ARElement.name: ARElement
ARElement.description: An element that can be defined stand-alone, i.e. without being part of another element (except for packages of course).

ARObject.name: ARObject
ARObject.description: Implicit base class of all classes in meta-model.

ARPackage.name: ARPackage
ARPackage.description:
AUTOSAR package, allowing to create top level packages to structure the contained ARElements.

ARPackages are open sets. This means that in a file based description system multiple files can be used to partially describe the contents of a package.

This is an extended version of MSR's SW-SYSTEM.

elements.name: referenceBases
elements.description: This denotes the reference bases for the package. This is the basis for all relative references within the package. The base needs to be selected according to the base attribute within the references.

elements.name: elements
elements.description:
Elements that are part of this package
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: arPackages
elements.description:
This represents a sub package within an ARPackage, thus allowing for an unlimited package hierarchy.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

AUTOSAR.name: AUTOSAR
AUTOSAR.description: Root element of an AUTOSAR description, also the root element in corresponding XML documents.

elements.name: adminData
elements.description: This represents the administrative data of an Autosar file.

elements.name: introduction
elements.description: This represents an introduction on the Autosar file. It is intended for example to rpresent disclaimers and legal notes.

elements.name: arPackages
elements.description:
This is the top level package in an AUTOSAR model.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: absolute
elements.description: Maximum allowable deviation in duration (in seconds)

AbstractCanCluster.name: AbstractCanCluster
AbstractCanCluster.description: Abstract class that is used to collect the common TtCAN, J1939 and CAN Cluster attributes.

AbstractCanClusterContent.name: AbstractCanClusterContent
AbstractCanClusterContent.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

elements.name: busOffRecovery
elements.description: CAN bus off monitoring / recovery at system level.

elements.name: canFdBaudrate
elements.description: Specifies the data segment baud rate of the controller in bits/s.

AbstractCanCommunicationConnector.name: AbstractCanCommunicationConnector
AbstractCanCommunicationConnector.description: Abstract class that is used to collect the common TtCAN and CAN CommunicationConnector attributes.

AbstractCanCommunicationController.name: AbstractCanCommunicationController
AbstractCanCommunicationController.description: Abstract class that is used to collect the common TtCAN and CAN Controller attributes.

AbstractCanCommunicationControllerAttrib.name: AbstractCanCommunicationControllerAttributes
AbstractCanCommunicationControllerAttrib.description:
For the configuration of the CanController parameters two different approaches can be used:
1. Providing exact values which are taken by the ECU developer (CanControllerConfiguration).
2. Providing ranges of values which are taken as requirements and have to be respected by the ECU developer (CanControllerConfigurationRequirements).

elements.name: canControllerFdAttributes
elements.description: Bit timing related configuration of a CAN controller for payload and CRC of a CanFD frame. If this element exists the controller supports CanFD frames and the ECU developer shall take these values for the configuration of the CanFD controller.

elements.name: canControllerFdRequirements
elements.description: Additional CanFD ranges of the bit timing related configuration of a CanFD controller. If this element exists the controller supports CanFD frames and the ECU developer shall take these ranges as requirements for the configuration of the CanFD controller.

AbstractCanCommunicationControllerConten.name: AbstractCanCommunicationControllerContent
AbstractCanCommunicationControllerConten.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

elements.name: canControllerAttributes
elements.description: CAN Bit Timing configuration

AbstractCanPhysicalChannel.name: AbstractCanPhysicalChannel
AbstractCanPhysicalChannel.description: Abstract class that is used to collect the common TtCAN and CAN PhysicalChannel attributes.

AbstractEvent.name: AbstractEvent
AbstractEvent.description: This meta-class represents the abstract ability to model an event that can be taken to implement application software or basic software in AUTOSAR.

elements.name: activationReasonRepresentationRef
elements.description: If the activationReasonRepresentation is referenced from the enclosing AbstractEvent this shall be taken as an indication that the latter contributes to the activating vector of this ExecutableEntity that owns the referenced ExecutableEntityActivationReason.

AbstractNumericalVariationPoint.name: AbstractNumericalVariationPoint
AbstractNumericalVariationPoint.description: This is an abstract NumericalValueVariationPoint. It is introduced to support the case that additional attributes are required for particular purposes.

AbstractProvidedPortPrototype.name: AbstractProvidedPortPrototype
AbstractProvidedPortPrototype.description: This abstract class provides the ability to become a provided PortPrototype.

elements.name: providedComSpecs
elements.description: Provided communication attributes per interface element (data element or operation).

AbstractRequiredPortPrototype.name: AbstractRequiredPortPrototype
AbstractRequiredPortPrototype.description: This abstract class provides the ability to become a required PortPrototype.

elements.name: requiredComSpecs
elements.description: Required communication attributes, one for each interface element.

AbstractRuleBasedValueSpecification.name: AbstractRuleBasedValueSpecification
AbstractRuleBasedValueSpecification.description: This represents an abstract base class for all rule-based value specifications.

AbstractServiceInstance.name: AbstractServiceInstance
AbstractServiceInstance.description: Provided and Consumed Ethernet Service Instances that are available at the ApplicationEndpoint.

elements.name: routingGroupRefs
elements.description: The ServiceDiscovery module is able to activate and deactivate the PDU routing from and to TCP/IP-sockets.

AclObjectSet.name: AclObjectSet
AclObjectSet.description:
This meta class represents the ability to denote a set of objects for which roles and rights (access control lists) shall be defined. It basically can define the objects based on

* the nature of objects
* the involved blueprints
* the artifact in which the objects are serialized
* the definition of the object (in a definition - value pattern)
* individual reference objects

elements.name: aclObjectClasss
elements.description: This specifies that the considered objects as instances of the denoted meta class.

elements.name: aclScope
elements.description: this indicates the scope of the referenced objects.

elements.name: collectionRef
elements.description: This indicates that the relevant objects are specified via a collection.

elements.name: derivedFromBlueprintRefs
elements.description: This association indicates that the considered objects are the ones being derived from the associated blueprint.

elements.name: engineeringObjects
elements.description:
This indicates an engineering object. The AclPermission relates to all objects in this partial model.

This also implies that the other objects in this set shall be placed in the specified engineering object. 

Note that semantic constraints apply with respect to <<atpSplitable>>

elements.name: objectDefinitionRefs
elements.description:
This denotes an object by its definition. For example the right to manipulate the value of a particular ecuc parameter is denoted by reference to the definition of the parameter.

Note that this can also be a reference to a Standard Module Definition. Therefore it is stereotyped by atpUriDef.

elements.name: objectDefintionRefs
elements.description:
Due to miss spell, this element was set to obsolete.
use instead: objectDefinition.

elements.name: objectRefs
elements.description: This association applies a particular (usually small) set of objects (e.g. a singular package). Main usage is, if one does not want to create a collection specifically for access control.

AclOperation.name: AclOperation
AclOperation.description: This meta class represents the ability to denote a particular operation which may be performed on objects in an AUTOSAR model.

elements.name: impliedOperationRefs
elements.description: This indicates that the related operations are also implied. Therefore the permission is also granted for this operation.

AclPermission.name: AclPermission
AclPermission.description: This meta class represents the ability to represent permissions granted on objects in an AUTOSAR model.

elements.name: aclContexts
elements.description:
This attribute is intended to specify the context under which the AclPemission is applicable. The values are subject to mutual agreement between the involved stakeholders.

For examples the values can be the names of binding times.

elements.name: aclObjectRefs
elements.description: This denotes an object to which the AclPermission applies.

elements.name: aclOperationRefs
elements.description: This denotes an operation which is granted by the given AclPermission.

elements.name: aclRoleRefs
elements.description: This denotes the role (individual or even organization) for which the AclPermission. is granted.

elements.name: aclScope
elements.description: This indicates the scope of applied permissions: explicit, descendant, dependent;

AclRole.name: AclRole
AclRole.description: This meta class represents the ability to specify a particular role which is used to grant access rights to AUTOSAR model. The purpose of this meta-class is to support the mutual agreements between the involved parties.

elements.name: ldapUrl
elements.description: This is an URL which allows to represent users or organizations taking the particular role.

AdminData.name: AdminData
AdminData.description:
AdminData represents the ability to express administrative information for an element. This administration information is to be treated as meta-data such as revision id or state of the file. There are basically four kinds of meta-data

* The language and/or used languages.

* Revision information covering e.g. revision number, state, release date, changes. Note that this information can be given in general as well as related to a particular company.

* Document meta-data specific for a company

elements.name: language
elements.description: This attribute  specifies the master language of the document or the document fragment. The master language is the one in which the document is maintained and from which the other languages are derived from. In particular in case of inconsistencies, the information in the master language is priority.

elements.name: usedLanguages
elements.description: This property specifies the languages which are provided in the document. Therefore it should only be specified in the top level admin data. For each language provided in the document there is one entry in MultilanguagePlainText. The content of each entry can be used for illustration of the language. The used language itself depends on the language attribute in the entry.

elements.name: docRevisions
elements.description:
This allows to denote information about the current revision of the object. 
Note that information about previous revisions can also be logged here. The entries shall be sorted descendant by date in order to reflect the history. Therefore the most recent entry representing the current version is denoted first.

elements.name: sdgs
elements.description: This property allows to keep special data which is not represented by the standard model. It can be utilized to keep e.g. tool specific data.

AgeConstraint.name: AgeConstraint
AgeConstraint.description:
The AgeConstraint is used to impose a constraint on an Timing Description Event referenced by the scope.

A minimum and a maximum age can be specified.

elements.name: maximum
elements.description: The maximum age.

elements.name: minimum
elements.description: The minimum age.

elements.name: scopeRef
elements.description: The scope of an AgeConstraint is any TimingDescriptionEvent that indicates any receipt of data.

AliasNameAssignment.name: AliasNameAssignment
AliasNameAssignment.description:
This meta-class represents the ability to associate an alternative name to a flat representations or an Identifiable.

The usage of this name is defined outside of AUTOSAR. For example this name can be used by MCD tools or as a name for component instances in the ECU extract.

Note that flatInstance and identifiable are mutually exclusive.

elements.name: shortLabel
elements.description: This attribute represents the alias name. It is modeled as string because the alias name is used outside of AUTOSAR and therefore no naming conventions can be applied within AUTOSAR.

elements.name: label
elements.description: This represents an "Alias LongName".

elements.name: identifiableRef
elements.description: Assignment of a unique name to an Identifiable.

elements.name: flatInstanceRef
elements.description: Assignment of a unique name to a flat representation.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

AliasNameSet.name: AliasNameSet
AliasNameSet.description:
This meta-class represents a set of AliasNames. The AliasNameSet can for example be an input to the A2L-Generator. It shall not be used by the RTE generator to generate the MC-Support.

In a given instance of AliasNameSet in the bound system there must be at most one aliasName per FlatInstanceDescriptor.

elements.name: aliasNames
elements.description:
AliasNames contained in the AliasNameSet.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

AnalyzedExecutionTime.name: AnalyzedExecutionTime
AnalyzedExecutionTime.description: AnalyzedExecutionTime provides an analytic method for specifying the best and worst case execution time.

elements.name: bestCaseExecutionTime
elements.description: The best case execution time (BCET) defines the minimum amount of time the related executable entity requires for its execution.

elements.name: worstCaseExecutionTime
elements.description: The worst case execution time (WCET) defines the maximum amount of time the related executable entity requires for its execution.

Annotation.name: Annotation
Annotation.description: This is a plain annotation which does not have further formal data.

AnyInstanceRef.name: AnyInstanceRef
AnyInstanceRef.description: Describes a reference to any instance in an AUTOSAR model. This is the most generic form of an instance ref. Refer to the superclass notes for more details.

elements.name: contextElementRef
elements.description: This is one step in the navigation path specified by the instance ref.

elements.name: targetRef
elements.description: This is the target of the instance ref.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

ApplicationArrayDataType.name: ApplicationArrayDataType
ApplicationArrayDataType.description: An application data type which is an array, each element is of the same application data type.

elements.name: dynamicArraySizeProfile
elements.description: Specifies the profile which the array will follow if it is a variable size array.

elements.name: element
elements.description: This association implements the concept of an array element. That is, in some cases it is necessary to be able to identify single array elements, e.g. as input values for an interpolation routine.

ApplicationArrayElement.name: ApplicationArrayElement
ApplicationArrayElement.description: Describes the properties of the elements of an application array data type.

elements.name: arraySizeHandling
elements.description: The way how the size of the array is handled.

elements.name: arraySizeSemantics
elements.description: This attribute controls how the information about the array size shall be interpreted.

elements.name: maxNumberOfElements
elements.description: The maximum number of elements that the array can contain.

ApplicationCompositeDataType.name: ApplicationCompositeDataType
ApplicationCompositeDataType.description: Abstract base class for all application data types composed of other data types.

ApplicationCompositeDataTypeSubElementRe.name: ApplicationCompositeDataTypeSubElementRef
ApplicationCompositeDataTypeSubElementRe.description: This meta-class represents the specialization of SubElementMapping with respect to ApplicationCompositeDataTypes.

elements.name: applicationCompositeElementIref
elements.description: This represents the referenced ApplicationCompositeDataPrototype.

ApplicationCompositeElementDataPrototype.name: ApplicationCompositeElementDataPrototype
ApplicationCompositeElementDataPrototype.description: This class represents a data prototype which is aggregated within a composite application data type (record or array). It is introduced to provide a better distinction between target and context in instanceRefs.

elements.name: typeTref
elements.description: This represents the corresponding data type.

elements.name: rootDataPrototypeRef
elements.description: This refers to the dataPrototype which is typed by theApplicationDatatype in which which the target can be found.

elements.name: contextDataPrototypeRef
elements.description: This represents a context ApplicationCompositeDataPrototype

elements.name: targetDataPrototypeRef
elements.description: This represents the referenced ApplicationCompositeDataPrototype.

ApplicationDataType.name: ApplicationDataType
ApplicationDataType.description:
ApplicationDataType defines a data type from the application point of view. Especially it should be used whenever something "physical" is at stake. 

An ApplicationDataType represents a set of values as seen in the application model, such as measurement units. It does not consider implementation details such as bit-size, endianess, etc.

It should be possible to model the application level aspects of a VFB system by using ApplicationDataTypes only.

ApplicationEndpoint.name: ApplicationEndpoint
ApplicationEndpoint.description: An application endpoint is the endpoint on an Ecu in terms of application addressing (e.g. socket). The application endpoint represents e.g. the listen socket in client-server-based communication.

elements.name: consumedServiceInstances
elements.description: Consumed service instances.

elements.name: discoveryTechnology
elements.description: Defines the used Service-Discovery protocol.

elements.name: networkEndpointRef
elements.description: Reference to the network address.

elements.name: priority
elements.description: Priority defined per application endpoint

elements.name: providedServiceInstances
elements.description: Provided service instances.

elements.name: remotingTechnology
elements.description: Defines the used remoting Technology.

elements.name: serializationTechnologyRef
elements.description: Defines the used serialization technology.

elements.name: tpConfiguration
elements.description: Configuration of the used transport protocol.

ApplicationEntry.name: ApplicationEntry
ApplicationEntry.description: Schedule table entry for application messages.

elements.name: frameTriggeringRef
elements.description: Specifies the LinFrame that will be transmitted in this frame slot.

ApplicationError.name: ApplicationError
ApplicationError.description: This is a user-defined error that is associated with an element of an AUTOSAR interface. It is specific for the particular functionality or service provided by the AUTOSAR software component.

elements.name: errorCode
elements.description: The RTE generator is forced to assign this value to the corresponding error symbol. Note that for error codes certain ranges are predefined (see RTE specification).

ApplicationErrorMapping.name: ApplicationErrorMapping
ApplicationErrorMapping.description:
In client server communication, the server may return any value within the application error range.

The ApplicationError is mapped to the responseGroup.

elements.name: systemSignalRef
elements.description: Reference to the SystemSignal with the ApplicationError.

ApplicationPrimitiveDataType.name: ApplicationPrimitiveDataType
ApplicationPrimitiveDataType.description: A primitive data type defines a set of allowed values.

ApplicationRecordDataType.name: ApplicationRecordDataType
ApplicationRecordDataType.description: An application data type which can be decomposed into prototypes of other application data types.

elements.name: elements
elements.description:
Specifies an element of a record.

The aggregation of ApplicationRecordElement is subject to variability with the purpose to support the conditional existence of elements inside a ApplicationrecordDataType.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

ApplicationRecordElement.name: ApplicationRecordElement
ApplicationRecordElement.description: Describes the properties of one particular element of an application record data type.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

ApplicationRuleBasedValueSpecification.name: ApplicationRuleBasedValueSpecification
ApplicationRuleBasedValueSpecification.description: This meta-class represents rule based values for DataPrototypes typed by ApplicationDataTypes (ApplicationArrayDataType or a compound ApplicationPrimitiveDataType which also boils down to an array-nature).

elements.name: category
elements.description: This represents the category of the RuleBasedValueSpecification

elements.name: swAxisConts
elements.description:
This represents the axis values of a Compound Primitive Data Type (curve or map).

The first swAxisCont describes the x-axis, the second swAxisCont describes the y-axis, the third swAxisCont describes the z-axis. In addition to this, the axis can be denoted in swAxisIndex.

elements.name: swValueCont
elements.description: This represents the values of an array or Compound Primitive Data Type.

ApplicationSwComponentType.name: ApplicationSwComponentType
ApplicationSwComponentType.description: The ApplicationSwComponentType is used to represent the application software.

ApplicationValueSpecification.name: ApplicationValueSpecification
ApplicationValueSpecification.description:
This meta-class represents values for DataPrototypes typed by ApplicationDataTypes (this includes in particular compound primitives). 

For further details refer to ASAM CDF 2.0. This meta-class corresponds to some extent with SW-INSTANCE in ASAM CDF 2.0.

elements.name: category
elements.description: Specifies to which category of ApplicationDataType this ApplicationValueSpecification can be applied (e.g. as an initial value), thus imposing constraints on the structure and semantics of the contained values, see [constr_1006] and [constr_2051].

elements.name: swAxisConts
elements.description:
This represents the axis values of a Compound Primitive Data Type (curve or map).

The first swAxisCont describes the x-axis, the second swAxisCont describes the y-axis, the third swAxisCont describes the z-axis. In addition to this, the axis can be denoted in swAxisIndex.

elements.name: swValueCont
elements.description: This represents the values of a Compound Primitive Data Type.

ArVariableInImplementationDataInstanceRe.name: ArVariableInImplementationDataInstanceRef
ArVariableInImplementationDataInstanceRe.description:
This class represents the ability to navigate into a data element inside of an VariableDataPrototype which is typed  by an ImplementationDatatype.

Note that it shall not be used if the target is the VariableDataPrototype itself (e.g. if its a primitive).

Note that this class follows the pattern of an InstanceRef but is not implemented based on the abstract classes because the ImplementationDataType isn't either, especially because ImplementationDataTypeElement isn't derived from AtpPrototype.

elements.name: portPrototypeRef
elements.description: This is the port providing/receiving the root of the variable

elements.name: rootVariableDataPrototypeRef
elements.description: This refers to the variableDataPrototype which is typed by the implementationDatatype in which which the target can be found.

elements.name: contextDataPrototypeRefs
elements.description: This is a context in case there are subelements with explicit types. The reference has to be ordered to properly reflect the nested structure.

elements.name: targetDataPrototypeRef
elements.description: This is a context in case there are subelements with explicit types.

ArbitraryEventTriggering.name: ArbitraryEventTriggering
ArbitraryEventTriggering.description:
The ArbitraryEventTriggering describes that an event occurs occasionally, singly, irregularly or randomly.

The primary purpose of this event triggering is to abstract event occurrences captured by data acquisition tools (background debugger, trace analyzer, etc.) during system runtime.

elements.name: minimumDistances
elements.description:
The nth array element describes the minimum distance that can be observed for a sample of n+1 event occurrences.

This is an array with an identical number of elements as for the maximumDistance.

elements.name: maximumDistances
elements.description:
The nth array element describes the maximum distance that can be observed for a sample of n+1 event occurrences.

This is an array with an identical number of elements as for the minimumDistance.

elements.name: confidenceIntervals
elements.description: List of confidence intervals.

Area.name: Area
Area.description:
This element specifies a region in an image map. Image maps enable authors to specify regions in an object (e.g. a graphic) and to assign a specific activity to each region (e.g. load a document, launch a program etc.).

For more details refer to the specification of HTML.

ArgumentDataPrototype.name: ArgumentDataPrototype
ArgumentDataPrototype.description: An argument of an operation, much like a data element, but also carries direction information and is owned by a particular ClientServerOperation.

elements.name: direction
elements.description: This attribute specifies the direction of the argument prototype.

elements.name: serverArgumentImplPolicy
elements.description:
This defines how the argument type of the servers RunnableEntity is implemented.

If the attribute is not defined this has the same semantics as if the attribute is set to the value useArgumentType for primitive arguments and structures and to the value useArrayBaseType for arrays.

elements.name: typeBlueprints
elements.description:
This allows to denote the intended type within blueprints. It shall be replaced by a proper type when deriving Interfaces from the Blueprint.
This property was modified due to atpVariation (DirectedAssociationPattern).

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

ArrayValueSpecification.name: ArrayValueSpecification
ArrayValueSpecification.description: Specifies the values for an array.

elements.name: elements
elements.description:
The value for a single array element. All ValueSpecifications aggregated by ArrayValueSpecification shall have the same structure.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

AssemblySwConnector.name: AssemblySwConnector
AssemblySwConnector.description: AssemblySwConnectors are exclusively used to connect SwComponentPrototypes in the context of a CompositionSwComponentType.

elements.name: providerIref
elements.description: Instance of providing port.

elements.name: requesterIref
elements.description: Instance of requiring port.

AssignFrameId.name: AssignFrameId
AssignFrameId.description: Schedule entry for an  Assign Frame Id master request.

elements.name: assignedFrameTriggeringRef
elements.description: The frame whose identifier is set by this assignment.

AssignFrameIdRange.name: AssignFrameIdRange
AssignFrameIdRange.description: AssignFrameIdRange generates an assign frame PID range request.

elements.name: framePids
elements.description: Optional assignment of frame_PID values that are included in the request. The frame_PIDs are ordered.

elements.name: startIndex
elements.description: The startIndex sets the index to the first frame to assign a PID.

AssignNad.name: AssignNad
AssignNad.description: Schedule entry for an Assign NAD master request.

elements.name: newNad
elements.description: The newly assigned NAD value.

AsynchronousServerCallPoint.name: AsynchronousServerCallPoint
AsynchronousServerCallPoint.description:
An AsynchronousServerCallPoint is used for asynchronous invocation of a ClientServerOperation.
IMPORTANT: a ServerCallPoint cannot be used concurrently. Once the client RunnableEntity has made the invocation, the ServerCallPoint cannot be used until the call returns (or an error occurs!) at which point the ServerCallPoint becomes available again.

AsynchronousServerCallResultPoint.name: AsynchronousServerCallResultPoint
AsynchronousServerCallResultPoint.description:
If a RunnableEntity owns a AsynchronousServerCallResultPoint it is entitled to get the result of the referenced AsynchronousServerCallPoint.
If it is associated with AsynchronousServerCallReturnsEvent, this RTEEvent notifies the completion of the required ClientServerOperation or a timeout. The occurrence of this event can either unblock a WaitPoint or can lead to the invocation of a RunnableEntity.

elements.name: asynchronousServerCallPointRef
elements.description: The referenced Asynchronous Server Call Point defines the asynchronous server call from which the results are returned.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

AsynchronousServerCallReturnsEvent.name: AsynchronousServerCallReturnsEvent
AsynchronousServerCallReturnsEvent.description: This event is raised when an asynchronous server call is finished.

elements.name: eventSourceRef
elements.description: The referenced AsynchronousServerCallResultPoint which is raises the RTEEvent in case of returning asynchronous server call.

AtomicSwComponentType.name: AtomicSwComponentType
AtomicSwComponentType.description: An atomic software component is atomic in the sense that it cannot be further decomposed and distributed across multiple ECUs.

elements.name: internalBehaviors
elements.description:
The SwcInternalBehaviors owned by an AtomicSwComponentType can be located in a different physical file. Therefore the aggregation is <<atpSplitable>>.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was 1.

elements.name: symbolProps
elements.description: This represents the SymbolProps for the AtomicSwComponentType.

AtpBlueprint.name: AtpBlueprint
AtpBlueprint.description: This meta-class represents the ability to act as a Blueprint. As this class is an abstract one, particular blueprint meta-classes inherit from this one.

elements.name: blueprintPolicys
elements.description: This role indicates whether the blueprintable element will be modifiable or not motifiable.

elements.name: shortNamePattern
elements.description:
This attribute represents the pattern which shall be used to build the shortName of the derived elements. As of now it is modeled as a String.  In general it should follow the pattern:

  pattern = (placeholder | namePart)*
  placeholder = "{" namePart "}"
  namePart = identifier | "_"

This is subject to be refined in subsequent versions.

Note that this is marked as obsolete. Use the xml attribute namePattern instead as it applies to Identifier and CIdentifier (shortName, symbol etc.)

AtpBlueprintMapping.name: AtpBlueprintMapping
AtpBlueprintMapping.description:
This meta-class represents the ability to express a particular mapping between a blueprint and an element derived from this blueprint.

Particular mappings are defined by specializations of this meta-class.

AtpBlueprintable.name: AtpBlueprintable
AtpBlueprintable.description: This meta-class represents the ability to be derived from a Blueprint. As this class is an abstract one, particular blueprintable meta-classes inherit from this one.

AtpClassifier.name: AtpClassifier
AtpClassifier.description: A classifier classifies M0 instances according to their features. Or: a classifier is something that has instances - an M1 classifier has M0 instances.

AtpDefinition.name: AtpDefinition
AtpDefinition.description: This abstract meta class represents "definition"-elements which identify the respective values. For example the value of a particular system constant is identified by the definition of this system constant.

AtpFeature.name: AtpFeature
AtpFeature.description: Features are properties via which a classifier classifies instances. Or: a classifier has features and every M0 instance of it will have those features.

AtpInstanceRef.name: AtpInstanceRef
AtpInstanceRef.description:
An M0 instance of a classifier may be represented as a tree rooted at that instance, where under each node come the sub-trees representing the instances which act as features under that node. 

An instance ref specifies a navigation path from any M0 tree-instance of the base (which is a classifier) to a leaf (which is an instance of the target).

AtpPrototype.name: AtpPrototype
AtpPrototype.description:
A prototype is a typed feature. A prototype in a classifier indicates that instances of that classifier will have a feature, and the structure of that feature is given by the its type. An instance of that type will play the role indicated by the feature in the owning classifier.

A feature is not an instance but an indication of an instance-to-be.

AtpStructureElement.name: AtpStructureElement
AtpStructureElement.description: A structure element is both a classifier and a feature. As a feature, its structure is given by the feature it owns as a classifier.

AtpType.name: AtpType
AtpType.description: A type is a classifier that may serve to type prototypes. It is a reusable classifier.

AttributeValueVariationPoint.name: AttributeValueVariationPoint
AttributeValueVariationPoint.description: This class represents the ability to derive the value of the Attribute from a system constant (by SwSystemconstDependentFormula). It also provides a bindingTime.

AutosarDataPrototype.name: AutosarDataPrototype
AutosarDataPrototype.description: Base class for prototypical roles of an AutosarDataType.

elements.name: typeTref
elements.description: This represents the corresponding data type.

AutosarDataType.name: AutosarDataType
AutosarDataType.description: Abstract base class for user defined AUTOSAR data types for ECU software.

elements.name: swDataDefProps
elements.description: The properties of this AutosarDataType.

This class represents a reference to an argument instance. This way it is possible to reference an argument instance in the occurrence expression formula. The argument instance can target to one of the following arguments:

* a whole argument used in an operation of a PortPrototype with ClientServerInterface

* an element inside of a composite argument used in an operation of a PortPrototype with ClientServerInterface

AutosarParameterRef.name: AutosarParameterRef
AutosarParameterRef.description:
This class represents a reference to a parameter within AUTOSAR which can be one of the following use cases:

localParameter:

* localParameter which is used as whole (e.g.  sharedAxis for curve)

autosarVariable:

* a parameter provided via PortPrototype which is used as whole (e.g. parameterAccess)

* an element inside of a composite local parameter typed by ApplicationDatatype (e.g. sharedAxis for a curve)

* an element inside of a composite parameter provided via Port and typed by ApplicationDatatype (e.g. sharedAxis for a curve)

autosarParameterInImplDatatype:

* an element inside of a composite local parameter typed by ImplementationDatatype

* an element inside of a composite parameter provided via PortPrototype and typed by ImplementationDatatype

elements.name: autosarParameterIref
elements.description: This instance reference is used if the callibration parameter is either imported via a port or is part of a composite data structure.

elements.name: localParameterRef
elements.description:
In the majority of cases this reference goes to ParameterDataPrototyoes rather than VariableDataPrototypes. Pointing the reference to a VariableDataPrototype is limited to special use cases, e.g. if the AutosarParameterRef is used in the context of an SwAxisGrouped.

This reference is used if the arParameter is local to the current component. 

Of course, it would technically also be feasible to use an InstanceRef for this case. However, the InstanceRef would not have a contextElement (because the cureent instance is the context).

Hence, the local instance is a special case which may provide further optimization. Therefore an explicit reference is provided for this case.

AutosarVariableInstance.name: AutosarVariableInstance
AutosarVariableInstance.description:
This class represents a reference to a variable instance within AUTOSAR. This way it is possible to reference a variable instance in the occurrence expression formula. The variable instance can target to one of the following variables:

* a variable provided via a PortPrototype as whole

* an element inside of a composite variable provided via a PortPrototype

elements.name: variableInstanceIref
elements.description: This is the reference to the instanceRef definition.

AutosarVariableRef.name: AutosarVariableRef
AutosarVariableRef.description:
This class represents a reference to a variable within AUTOSAR which can be one of the following use cases:

localVariable:

* localVariable which is used as whole (e.g. InterRunnableVariable, inputValue for curve)

autosarVariable:

* a variable provided via Port which is used as whole (e.g. dataAccesspoints)

* an element inside of a composite local variable typed by ApplicationDatatype (e.g. inputValue for a curve)

* an element inside of a composite variable provided via Port and typed by ApplicationDatatype (e.g. inputValue for a curve)

autosarVariableInImplDatatype:

* an element inside of a composite local variable typed by ImplementationDatatype  (e.g. nvramData mapping)

* an element inside of a composite variable provided via Port and typed by ImplementationDatatype (e.g. inputValue for a curve)

elements.name: autosarVariableInImplDatatype
elements.description: This is used if the target variable is inside of variableDataPrototype typed by an ImplementationDataType.

elements.name: autosarVariableIref
elements.description: This references a variable which is provided by a port and/or which is part of a CompositeDataType.

elements.name: localVariableRef
elements.description:
This reference is used if the variable is local to the current component. It would also be possible to use the instance refence here.
Such an instance ref would not have a contextElement, since the current instance is the context.
But the local instance is a special case which may provide further optimization. Therefore an expclicit reference is provided for this case.

BaseType.description: This abstract meta-class represents the ability to specify a platform dependant base type.

elements.name: baseTypeSize
elements.description: Describes the length of the data type specified in the container in bits.

elements.name: maxBaseTypeSize
elements.description: Describes the maximum length of the BaseType in bits.

elements.name: baseTypeEncoding
elements.description: This specifies, how an object of the current BaseType is encoded, e.g. in an ECU within a message sequence.

elements.name: memAlignment
elements.description: This attribute describes the alignment of the memory object in bits. E.g. "8" specifies, that the object in question is aligned to a byte while "32" specifies that it is aligned four byte. If the value is set to "0" the meaning shall be interpreted as "unspecified".

elements.name: byteOrder
elements.description: This attribute specifies the byte order of the base type.

elements.name: nativeDeclaration
elements.description:
This attribute describes the declaration of such a base type in the native programming language, primarily in the Programming language C. This can then be used by a code generator to include the necessary declarations into a header file. For example

BaseType with
   shortName: "MyUnsignedInt"
   nativeDeclaration: "unsigned short"

Results in

  typedef unsigned short MyUnsignedInt;

If the attribute is not defined the referring ImplementationDataTypes will not be generated as a typedef by RTE.

If a nativeDeclaration type is given it shall fulfill the characteristic given by basetypeEncoding and baseTypeSize.

This is required to ensure the consistent handling and interpretation by software components, RTE, COM and MCM systems.

elements.name: vendorApiInfix
elements.description:
In driver modules which can be instantiated several times on a single ECU, SRS_BSW_00347 requires that the names of files, APIs, published parameters and memory allocation keywords are extended by the vendorId and a vendor specific name. 
This parameter is used to specify the vendor specific name. In total, the implementation specific API name is generated as follows:
<ModuleName>_<vendorId>_ <vendorApiInfix>_<API name from SWS>.

E.g.  assuming that the vendorId of the implementer is 123 and the implementer chose a vendorApiInfix of "v11r456" an API name Can_Write defined in the SWS will translate to Can_123_v11r456_Write. 

This attribute is mandatory for all modules with upper multiplicity > 1. It shall not be used for modules with upper multiplicity =1.

See also SWS_BSW_00102.

* the vendor specific EcucModuleDef used in this BswImplementation if it represents a single module

* several EcucModuleDefs used in this BswImplementation if it  represents a cluster of modules

* one or no EcucModuleDefs used in this BswImplementation if it represents a library

BswModuleDependency.description: This class collects the dependencies of a BSW module or cluster on a certain other BSW module.

elements.description:
AUTOSAR identifier of the target module of which the dependencies are defined. 

This information is optional, because the target module may also be identified by targetModuleRef.

elements.name: targetModuleRefs
elements.description:
Reference to the target module. It is an <<atpUriDef>> because the reference shall be used to identify the target module without actually needing the description of that target module.
This property was modified due to atpVariation (DirectedAssociationPattern).

elements.name: requiredEntrys
elements.description:
Indicates an entry into another modules which is required by this module.
This property was modified due to atpVariation (DirectedAssociationPattern).

elements.name: expectedCallbacks
elements.description:
Indicates a callback expected to be called from another module and implemented by this module.
This property was modified due to atpVariation (DirectedAssociationPattern).

elements.name: serviceItems
elements.description:
A single item (example: Nv block) for which the quality of a service is defined.

The aggregation is marked as <<atpSplitable>> to allow for extension during the ECU configuration process.

This association is deprecated since R4.0.3, since ServiceNeeds shall be associated with the new element BswServiceDependency within the BswInternalBehavior.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

BswModuleDescription.name: BswModuleDescription
BswModuleDescription.description:
Root element for the description of a single BSW module or BSW cluster.
In case it describes a BSW module, the short name of this element equals the name of the BSW module.

elements.name: moduleId
elements.description: Refers to the BSW Module Identifier defined by the AUTOSAR standard. For non-standardized modules, a proprietary identifier can be optionally chosen.

elements.name: bswModuleDocumentations
elements.description:
This adds a documentation to the BSW module.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was 1.

elements.name: providedEntrys
elements.description:
Specifies an entry provided by this module which can be called by other modules. This includes "main" functions and interrupt routines, but not callbacks (because the signature of a callback is defined by the caller).
This property was modified due to atpVariation (DirectedAssociationPattern).

elements.name: outgoingCallbacks
elements.description:
Specifies a callback, which will be called from this module if required by 
another module.
This property was modified due to atpVariation (DirectedAssociationPattern).

elements.name: bswModuleDependencys
elements.description:
Describes the dependency to another BSW module.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: providedModeGroups
elements.description:
A set of modes which is owned and provided by this module or cluster. It can be connected to the requiredModeGroups of other modules or clusters via the configuration of the BswScheduler. It can also be synchronized with modes provided via ports by an associated ServiceSwComponentType, EcuAbstractionSwComponentType or ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: requiredModeGroups
elements.description:
Specifies that this module or cluster depends on a certain mode group. The requiredModeGroup is local to  this context and will be connected to the providedModeGroup of another module or cluster via the configuration of the BswScheduler.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: releasedTriggers
elements.description:
A Trigger released by this module or cluster. It can be connected to the requiredTriggers of other modules or clusters via the configuration of the BswScheduler. It can also be synchronized with Triggers provided via ports by an associated ServiceSwComponentType, EcuAbstractionSwComponentType or ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: requiredTriggers
elements.description:
Specifies that this module or cluster reacts upon an external trigger.This requiredTrigger is declared locally to this context and will be connected to the providedTrigger of another module or cluster via the configuration of the BswScheduler.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: providedClientServerEntrys
elements.description:
Specifies that this module provides a client server entry which can be called from another parition or core.This entry is declared locally to this context and will be connected to the requiredClientServerEntry of another or the same module via the configuration of the BSW Scheduler.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: requiredClientServerEntrys
elements.description:
Specifies that this module requires a client server entry which can be implemented on another parition or core.This entry is declared locally to this context and will be connected to the providedClientServerEntry of another or the same module via the configuration of the BSW Scheduler.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: providedDatas
elements.description:
Specifies a data prototype provided by this module in order to be read  from another partition or core.The providedData is declared locally to this context and will be connected to the requiredData of another or the same module via the configuration of the BSW Scheduler.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: requiredDatas
elements.description:
Specifies a data prototype required by this module in oder to be provided from another partition or core.The requiredData is declared locally to this context and will be connected to the providedData of another or the same module via the configuration of the BswScheduler.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: internalBehaviors
elements.description: The various BswInternalBehaviors associated with a BswModuleDescription can be distributed over several physical files. Therefore the aggregation is <<atpSplitable>>.

BswModuleDescriptionRefConditional.name: BswModuleDescriptionRefConditional
BswModuleDescriptionRefConditional.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

BswModuleEntity.name: BswModuleEntity
BswModuleEntity.description: Specifies the smallest code fragment which can be described for a BSW module or cluster within AUTOSAR.

elements.name: accessedModeGroups
elements.description:
A mode group which is accessed via API call by this entity. It must be a ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype required by this module or cluster.
This property was modified due to atpVariation (DirectedAssociationPattern).

elements.name: activationPoints
elements.description:
Activation point used by the module entity to activate one or more internal triggers.
This property was modified due to atpVariation (DirectedAssociationPattern).

elements.name: callPoints
elements.description:
A call point used in the code of this entitiy.

The variablity of this association is especially targeted at debug scenarios: It is possible to have one variant calling into the AUTOSAR debug module and another one which doesn't.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: calledEntrys
elements.description:
The entry of another (or the same) BSW module which is called by this entry (usually via C function call). This information allows to set up a model of call chains.

The variablity of this association is especially targeted at debug scenarios: It is possible to have one variant calling into the AUTOSAR debug module and another one which doesn't.

Note that this relation has been merked as obsolete, since the more powerful definition of a callPoint should be used.
This property was modified due to atpVariation (DirectedAssociationPattern).

elements.name: dataReceivePoints
elements.description:
The data is received via the BSW Scheduler.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: dataSendPoints
elements.description:
The data is sent via the BSW Scheduler.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: implementedEntryRef
elements.description: The entry which is implemented by this module entity.

elements.name: issuedTriggers
elements.description:
A trigger issued by this entity via BSW Scheduler API call. It must be a BswTrigger released (i.e. owned) by this module or cluster.
This property was modified due to atpVariation (DirectedAssociationPattern).

elements.name: managedModeGroups
elements.description:
A mode group which is managed by this entity. It must be a ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype provided by this module or cluster.
This property was modified due to atpVariation (DirectedAssociationPattern).

elements.name: schedulerNamePrefixRef
elements.description:
A prefix to be used in generated names for the BswModuleScheduler in the context of this BswModuleEntity, for example entry point prototypes, macros for dealing with exclusive areas, header file names.

Details are defined in the SWS RTE.

The prefix supersedes default rules for the prefix of those names.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

BswModuleEntry.name: BswModuleEntry
BswModuleEntry.description:
This class represents a single API entry (C-function prototype) into the BSW module or cluster.

The name of the C-function is equal to the short name of this element with one exception: In case of multiple instances of a module on the same CPU, special rules for "infixes" apply, see description of class BswImplementation.

elements.name: serviceId
elements.description: Refers to the service identifier of the Standardized Interfaces of AUTOSAR basic software. For non-standardized interfaces, it can optionally be used for proprietary identification.

elements.name: role
elements.description: Specifies the role of the entry in the given context. It shall be equal to the standardized name of the service call, especially in cases where no ServiceIdentifier is specified, e.g. for callbacks. Note that the ShortName is not always sufficient because it maybe vendor specific (e.g. for callbacks which can have more than one instance).

elements.name: isReentrant
elements.description:
Reentrancy from the viewpoint of function callers:

* True: Enables the service to be invoked again, before the service has finished.

* False: It is prohibited to invoke the service again before is has finished.

elements.name: isSynchronous
elements.description:
Synchronicity from the viewpoint of function callers:

* True: This calls a synchronous service, i.e. the service is completed when the call returns.

* False: The service (on semantical level) may not be complete when the call returns.

elements.name: callType
elements.description: The type of call associated with this service.

elements.name: executionContext
elements.description: Specifies the execution context which is required (in case of entries into this module) or guaranteed (in case of entries called from this module) for this service.

elements.name: swServiceImplPolicy
elements.description: Denotes the implementation policy as a standard function call, inline function or macro. This has to be specified on interface level because it determines the signature of the call.

elements.name: returnType
elements.description: The return type belonging to this bswModuleEntry.

elements.name: arguments
elements.description:
An argument belonging to this BswModuleEntry.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

BswModuleEntryRefConditional.name: BswModuleEntryRefConditional
BswModuleEntryRefConditional.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

BswModuleTiming.name: BswModuleTiming
BswModuleTiming.description:
A model element used to define timing descriptions and constraints for the BswInternalBehavior of one BSW Module. Thereby, for each BswInternalBehavior a separate timing can be specified.

A constraint defined at this level holds true for all Implementations of that BswInternalBehavior.

TimingDescriptions aggregated by BswModuleTiming are restricted to event chains referring to events which are derived from the class TDEventBswInternalBehavior.

elements.name: behaviorRef
elements.description: This defines the scope of a BswModuleTiming. All corresponding timing descriptions and constraints must be defined within this scope.

BswOperationInvokedEvent.name: BswOperationInvokedEvent
BswOperationInvokedEvent.description:
This event is thrown on operation invocation in Client-Server-Communication via the BSW Scheduler. Its "entry" reference provides the BswClientServerEntry that is called subsequently.

Note this event is not needed in case of direct function calls.

elements.name: entryRef
elements.description: The providedClientServerEntry invoked by this event.

BswParameterPolicy.name: BswParameterPolicy
BswParameterPolicy.description: The perInstanceParameter for which the BSW Scheduler using this policy.

elements.name: perInstanceParameterRef
elements.description: The perInstanceParameter for which the BSW Scheduler using this policy.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

elements.name: arTypedPerInstanceMemoryRef
elements.description: The arTypedPerInstanceMemory for which the BSW Scheduler using this policy

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

BswQueuedDataReceptionPolicy.name: BswQueuedDataReceptionPolicy
BswQueuedDataReceptionPolicy.description: Reception policy attributes specific for queued receiving.

elements.name: queueLength
elements.description: Length of queue for received events.

BswReleasedTriggerPolicy.name: BswReleasedTriggerPolicy
BswReleasedTriggerPolicy.description: The Trigger for which the BSW Scheduler using this policy.

elements.name: releasedTriggerRef
elements.description: The Trigger for which the BSW Scheduler using this policy.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

BswSchedulableEntity.name: BswSchedulableEntity
BswSchedulableEntity.description: BSW module entity, which is designed for control by the BSW Scheduler. It may for example implement a so-called "main" function.

BswScheduleEvent.name: BswScheduleEvent
BswScheduleEvent.description: BswEvent that is able to start a BswSchedulabeEntity.

BswSchedulerNamePrefix.name: BswSchedulerNamePrefix
BswSchedulerNamePrefix.description: A prefix to be used in names of generated code artifacts which make up the interface of a BSW module to the BswScheduler.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

BswServiceDependency.name: BswServiceDependency
BswServiceDependency.description: Specialization of ServiceDependency in the context of an BswInternalBehavior. It allows to associate BswModuleEntries and data defined for a BSW module or cluster to a given ServiceNeeds element.

elements.name: ident
elements.description: This adds the ability to become referrable to BswServiceDependency.

elements.name: assignedDatas
elements.description:
Defines the role of an associated data object (owned by this module or cluster) in the context of the ServiceNeeds element.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: assignedEntryRoles
elements.description:
Defines the role of an associated BswModuleEntry in the context of the ServiceNeeds element.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: serviceNeeds
elements.description: The associated ServiceNeeds.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

BswServiceDependencyIdent.name: BswServiceDependencyIdent
BswServiceDependencyIdent.description: This meta-class is created to add the ability to become the target of a reference to the non-Referrable BswServiceDependency.

BswSynchronousServerCallPoint.name: BswSynchronousServerCallPoint
BswSynchronousServerCallPoint.description: Represents a synchronous procedure call point via the BSW Scheduler.

elements.name: calledEntryRef
elements.description: The entry to be called.

elements.name: calledFromWithinExclusiveAreaRef
elements.description: This indicates that the call point is located at the deepest level inside one or more ExclusiveAreas that are nested in the given order.

BswTimingEvent.name: BswTimingEvent
BswTimingEvent.description: A recurring BswEvent driven by a time period.

elements.name: period
elements.description: Requirement for the time period (in seconds) by which this event is triggered.

BswTriggerDirectImplementation.name: BswTriggerDirectImplementation
BswTriggerDirectImplementation.description: Specifies a released trigger to be directly implemented via OS calls, for example in a Complex Driver module.

elements.name: masteredTriggerRef
elements.description:
The trigger which is directly mastered by this module.

There may be several different BswTriggerDirectImplementations mastering the same Trigger. This may be required e.g. due to memory partitioning.

elements.name: task
elements.description: The name of the OS task, which is controlled by the referred trigger. This means, that the module uses the trigger condition to directly activate an OS task instead of calling an API of the BswScheduler. The task name is required by the RTE generator resp. BswScheduler to raise the appropriate events in components or modules receiving the trigger.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

BswVariableAccess.name: BswVariableAccess
BswVariableAccess.description:
The presence of a BswVariableAccess implies that a BswModuleEntity needs access to a VariableDataPrototype via the BSW Scheduler.

The kind of access is specified by the role in which the class is used.

elements.name: accessedVariableRef
elements.description: The data accessed via the BSW Scheduler.

elements.name: contextLimitationRefs
elements.description: The existence of this reference indicates that the variable is recevied resp. sent only in the context of the referred BswDistinguishedPartitions.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

BufferProperties.name: BufferProperties
BufferProperties.description: Configuration of the buffer properties the transformer needs to work.

elements.name: bufferComputation
elements.description: If the transformer changes the size of the data, the CompuScale can be used to specify a rule to derive the size of the output data based on the size of the input data.

elements.name: headerLength
elements.description: Defines the length of the header (in bits) this transformer will add in front of the data.

elements.name: inPlace
elements.description: If set, the transformer uses the input buffer as output buffer.

BuildAction.name: BuildAction
BuildAction.description: This meta-class represents the ability to specify a build action.

elements.name: predecessorActionRefs
elements.description:
This association specifies a set of predecessors. These actions must be finished before but necessarily immediately after the given action..

These actions need to be performed in the specified order.

elements.name: followUpActionRefs
elements.description: This association specifies a set of follow up actions.

elements.name: createdDatas
elements.description: This represents the artifacts which are cated by the processor.

elements.name: inputDatas
elements.description: This represents the artifacts which are read by the processor.

elements.name: modifiedDatas
elements.description: This denotes the data which are modifed by the action.

elements.name: requiredEnvironmentRef
elements.description: This represents the environment which is required to use the specified Processor.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

BuildActionEntity.name: BuildActionEntity
BuildActionEntity.description: This meta-class represents the ability to describe a build action entity which might be specialized to environments as well as to individual build actions.

elements.name: deliveryArtifacts
elements.description: This denotes the delivery artifacts for the entity for reference purposes.

elements.name: invocation
elements.description: This specifies how to invoke a build action in the given environment.

BuildActionEnvironment.name: BuildActionEnvironment
BuildActionEnvironment.description: This meta-class represents the ability to specify a build action environment.

elements.name: sdgs
elements.description: This represents a general data structure  intended to denote parameters for the BuildActionEnvironment.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

BuildActionInvocator.name: BuildActionInvocator
BuildActionInvocator.description: This meta-class represents the ability to specify the invocation of a task in a build action.

elements.name: command
elements.description:
This represents the command to invocate the processor. Note that this is a generic string which can be interpreted properly in the processor environment.

Note that it is optional due to the fact that some actions are hardwired in the environment and do not need an explicit command.

On the other hand the properties of an invocator can be complex and not standardized.

elements.name: sdgs
elements.description: This represents a general data structure  intended to denote parameters for the BuildAction.

BuildActionIoElement.name: BuildActionIoElement
BuildActionIoElement.description: This meta-class represents the ability to specify the input/output entities of a BuildAction.

elements.name: category
elements.description:
This element assigns a category to the parent element. It is intended to specialize the usage and/or the content of the object. Such a specialization may also impose particular semantic constraints on the entire substructure.

See also Identifiable.

elements.name: sdgs
elements.description: This special data group allows to denote specific data. The structure is subject of mutual agreement.

elements.name: ecucDefinitionRef
elements.description:
This association denotes an ECUC parameter definition. The such referenced parameters are subject of the build action input/ouptut.

Note that the reference to the definition denotes the right for a build action to read and/or write values for the given defintion and all contained definitions.

elements.name: engineeringObject
elements.description: This represents an artifact applicable to the build action.

elements.name: foreignModelReference
elements.description: This is a reference to a foreign model element. Note that it is not modeled as an association because it should also be able to refer also to non AUTOSAR models.

elements.name: modelObjectReference
elements.description: This is a reference to a generic model element. Note that it is not modeled as an association because it should also be able to refer also to non AUTOSAR models.

elements.name: role
elements.description: This attribute allows to denote a particular role of the collection. Note that the applicable semantics shall be mutually agreed between the two parties.

BuildActionManifest.name: BuildActionManifest
BuildActionManifest.description: This meta-class represents the ability to specify a manifest for processing artifacts. An example use case is the processing of ECUC parameter values.

elements.name: startActionRefs
elements.description: This specifies the list of actions to be performed at the beginning of the process.

elements.name: tearDownActionRefs
elements.description: This specifies the set of action which shall be performed after all other actions in the manifest were performed.

elements.name: buildActions
elements.description:
This represents a particular action in the build chain.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: buildActionEnvironments
elements.description:
This represents a build action environment.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: dynamicActionRefs
elements.description: This denots an Action which is to be executed as part of the dynamic action set.

BuildActionManifestRefConditional.name: BuildActionManifestRefConditional
BuildActionManifestRefConditional.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

BuildEngineeringObject.name: BuildEngineeringObject
BuildEngineeringObject.description: This meta-class represents the ability to denote an artifact which is processed within a particular build action.

elements.name: fileType
elements.description: This attribute indicates the file type which shall used for the engineering object. Note that an engineering object may deliver multiple representations of the same artifact. This attribute can select one of the provided representations.

elements.name: intendedFilename
elements.description:
This attribute represents the name of the file if it is created newly. Note that engineering object resolves category + ShortLabel indicate mainly to refer to an existing file. If the file is created newly, the filename can either be determined by built in policy or predefined here. 

Note that extensions shall part of file name even if it could be derived from fileType.

elements.name: parentCategory
elements.description: This represents the category of the parent object.

elements.name: parentShortLabel
elements.description: This represents the shortLabel of the parent object. This allows to specify the output position in a hierarchically organized sysyetm

elements.name: shortLabelPattern
elements.description: This attribute allows to define a set of engineering objects as pattern based search applied to the shortLabel of the individual Enginering objects.

elements.name: fileTypePattern
elements.description: This attribute allows to define a set of engineering objects as pattern based search applied to the filetype of the individual Engineering objects.

BurstPatternEventTriggering.name: BurstPatternEventTriggering
BurstPatternEventTriggering.description:
A BurstPatternEventTriggering describes the maximum number of occurrences of the same event in a given time interval.
This is typically used to model a worst case activation scenario.

elements.name: maxNumberOfOccurrences
elements.description: The maximum number of event occurrences within the given time interval.

elements.name: minimumInterArrivalTime
elements.description: The parameter “Minimum Inter-Arrival Time” specifies the minimum distance between subsequent occurrences of the event within the given time interval.

elements.name: patternJitter
elements.description: The optional parameter “Pattern Jitter” specifies the deviation of the time interval’s starting point from the beginning of the given period. This parameter is only applicable in conjunction with the parameter “Pattern Period”.

elements.name: patternLength
elements.description: The parameter “Pattern Length” specifies the duration of the time interval within which the event repeatedly occurs. The event occurs at arbitrary points in time within the given time interval.

elements.name: patternPeriod
elements.description: The optional parameter “Pattern Period” specifies the time distance between the beginnings of subsequent repetitions of the given burst pattern.

elements.name: minNumberOfOccurrences
elements.description: The minimum number of event occurrences within the given time interval.

CalibrationParameterValue.name: CalibrationParameterValue
CalibrationParameterValue.description:
Specifies instance specific calibration parameter values used to initialize the memory objects implementing calibration parameters in the generated RTE code.

RTE generator will use the implInitValue to override the initial values specified for the DataPrototypes of a component type. 

The applInitValue is used to exchange init values with the component vendor not publishing the transformation algorithm between ApplicationDataTypes and ImplementationDataTypes or defining a instance specific initialization of components which are only defined with ApplicationDataTypes.

Note: If both representations of init values are available these need to represent the same content.

Note further that in this case an explicit mapping of ValueSpecification is not implemented because calibration parameters are delivered back after the calibration phase.

elements.name: applInitValue
elements.description: This is the initial value specification structured according to the ApplicationDataType

elements.name: implInitValue
elements.description: This is the initial value specification structured according to the ImplementationDataType

elements.name: initializedParameterRef
elements.description: This represents the parameter that is initialized by the CalibrationParameterValue.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

CalibrationParameterValueSet.name: CalibrationParameterValueSet
CalibrationParameterValueSet.description: Specification of a constant that can be part of a package, i.e. it can be defined stand-alone.

elements.name: calibrationParameterValues
elements.description:
This represents single CalibrationParameterValues in the CalibrationParameterValueSet.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: canClusterVariants
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

CanClusterBusOffRecovery.name: CanClusterBusOffRecovery
CanClusterBusOffRecovery.description: This element contains the attributes that are used to configure the CAN bus off monitoring / recovery at system level.

elements.name: borCounterL1ToL2
elements.description: This threshold defines the count of bus-offs until the bus-off recovery switches from level 1 (short recovery time) to level 2 (long recovery time).

elements.name: borTimeL1
elements.description: This attribute defines the duration of the bus-off recovery time in level 1 (short recovery time) in seconds.

elements.name: borTimeL2
elements.description: This attribute defines the duration of the bus-off recovery time in level 2 (long recovery time) in seconds.

elements.name: borTimeTxEnsured
elements.description: This attribute defines the duration of the bus-off event check in seconds.

elements.name: mainFunctionPeriod
elements.description: This attribute defines the cycle time of the function CanSM_MainFunction in seconds.

CanClusterConditional.name: CanClusterConditional
CanClusterConditional.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

CanClusterContent.name: CanClusterContent
CanClusterContent.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

CanCommunicationConnector.name: CanCommunicationConnector
CanCommunicationConnector.description: CAN bus specific communication connector attributes.

elements.name: pncWakeupCanId
elements.description: CAN Identifier used to configure the CAN Transceiver for partial network wakeup.

elements.name: pncWakeupCanIdExtended
elements.description: Defines whether pncWakeupCanId and pncWakeupCanIdMask shall be interpreted as extended or standard CAN ID.

elements.name: pncWakeupCanIdMask
elements.description: Bit mask for CAN Identifier used to configure the CAN Transceiver for partial network wakeup.

elements.name: pncWakeupDataMask
elements.description:
Bit mask for CAN Payload used to configure the CAN Transceiver for partial network wakeup.

This attribute should not be computed from the pncIdentifier values in order to support future introduction of additional PNCs. 

Note that for one EcuInstance all contributing pncWakeupDataMask will be bitwise ORed to obtain the value of CanNmPnFilterMaskByte. Note that this data mask is calculated over the whole payload (8 Byte) of the NmPdu ignoring the leading bytes which do not contain pncVector information. The number of leading bytes which shall be ignored is equivalent to the value of System.pncVectorOffset.

elements.name: pncWakeupDlc
elements.description: Data Length of the remote data frame used to configure the CAN Transceiver for partial network wakeup in Bytes.

CanCommunicationController.name: CanCommunicationController
CanCommunicationController.description: CAN bus specific communication port attributes.

elements.description: Specifies propagation delay in time quantas.

elements.name: syncJumpWidth
elements.description: The number of quanta in the Synchronization Jump Width, SJW. The (Re-)Synchronization Jump Width (SJW) defines how far a resynchronization may move the Sample Point inside the limits defined by the Phase Buffer Segments to compensate for edge phase errors.

elements.name: timeSeg1
elements.description:

timeSeg1 = Phase_Seg1

elements.name: timeSeg2
