CanControllerConfigurationRequirements.name: CanControllerConfigurationRequirements
CanControllerConfigurationRequirements.description: This element allows the specification of ranges for the CAN Bit Timing configuration parameters. These ranges are taken as requirements and have to be respected by the ECU developer.

elements.name: maxNumberOfTimeQuantaPerBit
elements.description: Maximum number of time quanta in the bit time.

elements.name: maxSamplePoint
elements.description: The max. value of the sample point as a percentage of the total bit time.

elements.name: maxSyncJumpWidth
elements.description: The max. Synchronization Jump Width value as a percentage of the total bit time. The (Re-)Synchronization Jump Width (SJW) defines how far a resynchronization may move the Sample Point inside the limits defined by the Phase Buffer Segments to compensate for edge phase errors.

elements.name: minNumberOfTimeQuantaPerBit
elements.description: Minimum number of time quanta in the bit time.

elements.name: minSamplePoint
elements.description: The min. value of the sample point as a percentage of the total bit time.

elements.name: minSyncJumpWidth

CanControllerFdConfiguration.name: CanControllerFdConfiguration
CanControllerFdConfiguration.description: Bit timing related configuration of a CAN controller for payload and CRC of a CAN FD frame.

elements.name: paddingValue
elements.description: Specifies the value which is used to pad unused data in CAN FD frames which are bigger than 8 byte if the length of a Pdu which was requested to be sent does not match the allowed DLC values of CAN FD.

elements.name: txBitRateSwitch

TRUE: CAN FD frames shall be sent with bit rate switching.
FALSE: CAN FD frames shall be sent without bit rate switching.

CanFrame.name: CanFrame
CanFrame.description: CAN specific Frame element. This element shall also be used for TTCan.

CanFrameTriggering.name: CanFrameTriggering
CanFrameTriggering.description: CAN specific attributes to the FrameTriggering

elements.name: absolutelyScheduledTimings
elements.description: Each frame in TTCAN is identified by its slot id and communication cycle. A description is provided by the usage of AbsolutelyScheduledTiming.

elements.name: canAddressingMode
elements.description: The CAN protocol supports two types of frame formats. The standard frame format uses 11-bit identifiers and is defined in the CAN specification 2.0 A. Additionally the extended frame format allows 29-bit identifiers and is defined in the CAN specification 2.0 B.

elements.name: canFdFrameSupport
elements.description: This attribute describes whether the CAN FD option is activated or not. If this attribute is TRUE this frame can be sent/received as CAN FD frame. Otherwise it has to be CAN 2.0 compliant.

elements.name: canFrameRxBehavior
elements.description: Defines which CAN protocol shall be expected for frame reception.

elements.name: canFrameTxBehavior
elements.description: Defines which CAN protocol shall be used for frame transmission.

elements.name: identifier
elements.description: To describe a frames identifier on the communication system, usually with a fixed identifierValue. In a complete system description this attribute is mandatory. In an Ecu Extract for the sender of the frame the identifier shall also be provided. In an Ecu Extract for the receiver the identifier attribute shall be ignored if rxIdentifierRange is defined.

elements.name: j1939Requestable
elements.description: Frame can be triggered by the J1939 request message.

elements.name: rxIdentifierRange
elements.description: Optional definition of a CanId range.

elements.name: rxMask
elements.description: Identifier mask which denotes the relevant bits in the CAN Identifier. Together with the identifier, this parameter defines a CAN identifier range.

elements.name: txMask
elements.description: Identifier mask which denotes static bits in the CAN identifier. The other bits can be set dynamically.

elements.name: nmBusloadReductionActive
elements.description: It determines if bus load reduction for the respective CanNm channel is active or not.

elements.name: nmCarWakeUpBitPosition
elements.description: Specifies the bit position of the CarWakeUp within the NmPdu.

elements.name: nmCarWakeUpFilterEnabled
elements.description:
Please note that this parameter is deprecated and will be removed in future. 

Old description:
If this attribute is set to true the CareWakeUp filtering is supported. In this case only the CarWakeUp bit within the NmPdu with source node identifier nmCarWakeUpFilterNodeId is considered as CarWakeUp request.

elements.name: nmCarWakeUpFilterNodeId
elements.description: Source node identifier for CarWakeUp filtering. If CarWakeUp filtering is supported (nmCarWakeUpFilterEnabled), only the CarWakeUp bit within the NmPdu with source node identifier nmCarWakeUpFilterNodeId is considered as CarWakeUp request.

elements.name: nmCarWakeUpRxEnabled
elements.description:
Please note that this parameter is deprecated and will be removed in future.

Old description:
If set to true this attribute enables the support of CarWakeUp bit evaluation in received NmPdus.

elements.name: nmCbvPosition
elements.description: Defines the position of the control bit vector within the NmPdu (Byte position). If this attribute is not configured, the Control Bit Vector is not used.

elements.name: nmChannelActive
elements.description:
Please note that this attribute is deprecated and will be removed in future.

This switch determines if the respective CanNm channel is active or not. Indicates whether a particular CanNm channel shall be initialized (TRUE) or not (FALSE). If this parameter is set to FALSE the respective NM instance shall not be used during runtime.

elements.name: nmImmediateNmCycleTime
elements.description: Defines the immediate NmPdu cycle time in seconds which is used for nmImmediateNmTransmissions NmPdu transmissions. This parameter is only valid if CanNmImmediateNmTransmissions is greater one.

elements.name: nmImmediateNmTransmissions
elements.description: Defines the number of immediate NmPdus which shall be transmitted. If the value is zero no immediate NmPdus are transmitted. The cycle time of immeditate NmPdus is defined by nmImmediateNmCycleTime.

elements.name: nmMessageTimeoutTime
elements.description: Timeout of an NmPdu in seconds. It determines how long the NM shall wait with notification of transmission failure while communication errors occur on the bus.

elements.name: nmMsgCycleTime
elements.description: Period of a NmPdu in seconds. It determines the periodic rate in the periodic transmission mode with bus load reduction and is the basis for transmit scheduling in the periodic transmission mode without bus load reduction.

elements.name: nmNetworkTimeout
elements.description:
Network Timeout for NmPdus in seconds
It denotes the time how long the CanNm shall stay in the Network Mode before transition into Prepare Bus-Sleep Mode shall take place.

elements.name: nmNidPosition
elements.description: Defines the byte position of the source node identifier within the NmPdu. If this attribute is not configured, the Node Identification is not used.

elements.name: nmRemoteSleepIndicationTime
elements.description: Timeout for Remote Sleep Indication in seconds. It defines the time how long it shall take to recognize that all other nodes are ready to sleep.

elements.name: nmRepeatMessageTime
elements.description: Timeout for Repeat Message State in seconds. Defines the time how long the NM shall stay in the Repeat Message State.

elements.name: nmUserDataLength
elements.description:
Defines the length of the user data contained in the NmPdu.

Please note that this attribute is deprecated and will be removed in future.

elements.name: nmWaitBusSleepTime
elements.description: Timeout for bus calm down phase in seconds. It denotes the time how long the CanNm shall stay in the Prepare Bus-Sleep Mode before transition into Bus-Sleep Mode shall take place.

CanNmClusterCoupling.name: CanNmClusterCoupling
CanNmClusterCoupling.description: CAN attributes that are valid for each of the referenced (coupled) CAN clusters.

elements.name: coupledClusterRefs
elements.description: Reference to coupled CAN Clusters.

elements.name: nmBusloadReductionEnabled
elements.description: Enables busload reduction support

elements.name: nmImmediateRestartEnabled
elements.description: Enables the asynchronous transmission of a CanNm PDU upon bus-communication request in Prepare-Bus-Sleep mode.

elements.name: nmRepeatMsgIndicationEnabled
elements.description: Enable/disable the notification that a RepeatMessageRequest bit has been received. This attribute is deprecated and shall be not used. It will be removed in the future. The nmRepeatMsgIndEnabled attribute in NmEcu shall be used instead.

elements.name: nmCarWakeUpFilterEnabled
elements.description: If this attribute is set to true the CareWakeUp filtering is supported. In this case only the CarWakeUp bit within the NmPdu with source node identifier nmCarWakeUpFilterNodeId is considered as CarWakeUp request.

elements.name: nmCarWakeUpRxEnabled
elements.description: If set to true this attribute enables the support of CarWakeUp bit evaluation in received NmPdus.

elements.name: nmMsgCycleOffset
elements.description: Node specific time offset in the periodic transmission node. It determines the start delay of the transmission. Specified in seconds.

elements.name: nmMsgReducedTime
elements.description: Node specific bus cycle time in the periodic transmission mode with bus load reduction. Specified in seconds.

elements.name: nmRangeConfig
elements.description:
Defines the CANID ranges that are used for Nm. 
This range definition is redundant to the attribute "rxIdentifierRange" of CanFrameTriggering. For backward compatibility reasons this redundancy shall be preserved and both shall be defined. In future this element will be removed from the model.

CanNmRangeConfig.name: CanNmRangeConfig
CanNmRangeConfig.description:
Defines the CANID ranges that are used for Nm. This range definition is redundant to the attribute "rxIdentifierRange" of CanFrameTriggering. For backward compatibility reasons this redundancy shall be preserved and both shall be defined.
In future this element will be removed from the model.

CanTpConnection.name: CanTpConnection
CanTpConnection.description:
A connection identifies the sender and the receiver of this particular communication. The CanTp module routes a Pdu through this connection. 

atpVariation: Derived, because TpNode can vary.

elements.name: addressingFormat
elements.description: Declares which communication addressing mode is supported.

elements.name: canTpChannelRef
elements.description: Reference to the CanTpChannel on which this CanTpConnection is realized.

elements.name: cancellation
elements.description: With this switch Tx and Rx Cancellation can be turned on or off.

elements.name: dataPduRef
elements.description: Reference to an Data NPdu.

elements.name: flowControlPduRef
elements.description: Reference to the Flow Control NPdu.

elements.name: maxBlockSize
elements.description:
The maximum number of N-PDUs the CanTp receiver allows the sender to send, before waiting for an authorization to continue transmission of the following N-PDUs. For further details on this parameter value see ISO 15765-2 specification.

Note: For reasons of buffer length, the CAN Transport Layer can adapt the BS value within the limit of this maximum BS

elements.name: multicastRef
elements.description: TP address for 1:n connections.

elements.name: paddingActivation
elements.description:
This specifies wheter or not Sfs, FCs and the last CF shall be padded to 8 bytes length in case it contains less payload.

true:
The N-PDU received uses padding for SF, FC and the last CF. (N-PDU length is always 8 bytes)

false:
The N-PDU received does not use padding for SF, CF and the last CF. (N-PDU length is dynamic)

elements.name: receiverRefs
elements.description: The target of the TP connection.

elements.name: taType
elements.description: Network Target Address type.

elements.name: timeoutBr
elements.description: Value in seconds of the performance requirement for (N_Br + N_Ar). N_Br is the elapsed time between the receiving indication of a FF or CF or the transmit confirmation of a FC, until the transmit request of the next FC.

elements.name: timeoutBs
elements.description: This parameter defines the timout for waiting for an FC or AF on the sender side in an 1:1 connection. Specified in seconds.

elements.name: timeoutCr
elements.description: This parameter defines the timeout value for waiting for a CF or FF-x (in case of retry) after receiving the last CF or after sending an FC or AF on the receiver side. Specified in seconds.

elements.name: timeoutCs
elements.description: The attribute timeoutCs represents the time (in seconds) which elapses between the transmit request of a CF N-PDU until the transmit request of the next CF N-PDU.

elements.name: tpSduRef
elements.description: Reference to an IPdu that is segmented by the Transport Protocol.

elements.name: transmitCancellation
elements.description:
With this switch Transmit Cancellation can be turned on or off for this channel.

Please note that this attribute is deprecated and will be removed in future.

elements.name: transmitterRef
elements.description: The source of the TP connection.

CanTpNode.name: CanTpNode
CanTpNode.description: TP Node (Sender or Receiver) provides the TP Address and the connection to the Topology description.

elements.name: connectorRef
elements.description:
Asscociation to a CommunicationConnector in the topology description. 
In a System Description this reference is mandatory. In an ECU Extract this reference is optional (references to ECUs that are not part of the ECU Extract shall be avoided).

elements.name: maxFcWait
elements.description: This attribute defines the maximum number of flow control PDUs that can be consecutively be transmitted by a receiver.

elements.name: stMin
elements.description: Sets the duration of the minimum time the CanTp sender shall wait between the transmissions of two CF N-PDUs.

elements.name: timeoutAr
elements.description: This attribute states the timeout between the PDU transmit request of the Transport Layer to the Can Interface and the corresponding confirmation of the Can Interface on the receiver side (for FC or AF). Specified in seconds.

elements.name: timeoutAs
elements.description: This attribute states the timeout between the PDU transmit request for the first PDU of the group used in the current connection of the Transport Layer to the Can Interface and the corresponding confirmation of the Can Interface (when having sent the last PDU of the group used in this connection) on the sender side (SF-x, FF-x, CF or FC (in case of Transmit Cancellation)). Specified in seconds.

elements.name: tpAddressRef
elements.description: Reference to the TP Address that is used by the TpNode. This reference is optional in case that the multicast TP Address is used (reference from TpConnection).

ClientComSpec.description: Client-specific communication attributes (RPortPrototype typed by ClientServerInterface).

elements.name: operationRef
elements.description: This represents the corresponding ClientServerOperation.

elements.name: transformationComSpecPropss
elements.description: This references the TransformationComSpecProps which define port-specific configuration for data transformation.

ClientIdDefinition.name: ClientIdDefinition
ClientIdDefinition.description:
Several clients in one client-ECU can communicate via inter-ECU client-server communication with a server on a different ECU, if a client identifier is used to distinguish the different clients.
The Client Identifier of the transaction handle that is used by the RTE can be defined by this element.

elements.name: clientId
elements.description: The Client Identifier of the transaction handle used for a inter-ECU client server communication is defined by this attribute. If defined the RTE generator shall use this clientId.

elements.name: clientServerOperationIref
elements.description: Reference to the ClientServerOperation that is called by the client.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

ClientIdDefinitionSet.name: ClientIdDefinitionSet
ClientIdDefinitionSet.description: Set of Client Identifiers that are used for inter-ECU client-server communication in the System.

elements.name: clientIdDefinitions
elements.description: The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

ClientIdMapping.name: ClientIdMapping
ClientIdMapping.description:
In case of a server on one ECU with multiple clients on other ECUs, the client server communication shall use different unique COM signals and signal groups for each client to allow the identification of the client associated with each system signal.

The ClientId is mapped to the requestGroup and to the responseGroup.

elements.name: systemSignalRef
elements.description: Reference to the SystemSignal with the ClientID.

ClientIdRange.name: ClientIdRange
ClientIdRange.description: With this element it is possible to restrict the Client Identifier of the transaction handle that is generated by the client RTE for inter-Ecu Client/Server communication to an allowed range of numerical values.

elements.name: lowerLimit
elements.description: This specifies the lower limit of the ClientIdRange.

elements.name: upperLimit
elements.description: This specifies the upper limit of the ClientIdRange.

ClientServerAnnotation.name: ClientServerAnnotation
ClientServerAnnotation.description: Annotation to a port regarding a certain Operation.

elements.name: operationRef
elements.description: This represents the ClientServerOperation that the ClientServerAnnotation corresponds to.

ClientServerApplicationErrorMapping.name: ClientServerApplicationErrorMapping
ClientServerApplicationErrorMapping.description: This meta-class represents the ability to map ApplicationErrors onto each other.

elements.name: firstApplicationErrorRef
elements.description: This represents the first ApplicationError in the context of the ClientServerApplicationErrorMapping.

elements.name: secondApplicationErrorRef
elements.description: This represents the second ApplicationError in the context of the ClientServerApplicationErrorMapping.

ClientServerArrayElementMapping.name: ClientServerArrayElementMapping
ClientServerArrayElementMapping.description:
The ApplicationArrayElement may be a primitive one or a composite one. If the element is primitive, it will be mapped to the "SystemSignal" (multiplicity 1). If the ArgumentDataPrototype that is referenced by ClientServerCompositeTypeMapping is typed by an ApplicationDataType the reference to the ApplicationArrayElement shall be used. If the VariableDataPrototype is typed by the ImplementationDataType the reference to the ImplementationArrayElement shall be used. 

If the element is composite, there will be no mapping to the "SystemSignal" (multiplicity 0). In this case the "ArrayElementMapping" Element will aggregate the "TypeMapping" Element. In that way also the composite datatypes can be mapped to SystemSignals. 

Regardless whether composite or primitive array element is mapped the indexed array element always needs to be specified.

elements.name: complexTypeMapping
elements.description: This aggregation will be used if the element is  composite.

elements.name: indexedArrayElement
elements.description: Reference to an indexed array element in the context of the mappedOperation or in the context of a composite element.

elements.name: systemSignalRef
elements.description: Reference to the system signal used to carry the primitive ApplicationArrayElement.

ClientServerArrayTypeMapping.name: ClientServerArrayTypeMapping
ClientServerArrayTypeMapping.description: If the ApplicationCompositeDataType is an Array, the "ArrayTypeMapping" will be used.

elements.name: arrayElementMappings
elements.description: Each ApplicationArrayElement must be mapped on a SystemSignal.

ClientServerCompositeTypeMapping.name: ClientServerCompositeTypeMapping
ClientServerCompositeTypeMapping.description:
Two mappings exist for the composite data types: "ArrayTypeMapping" and "RecordTypeMapping".
In both, a primitive datatype will be mapped to a system signal. 

But it is also possible to combine the arrays and the records, so that an "array" could be an element of a "record" and in the same manner a "record" could be an element of an "array". Nesting these data types is also possible.

If an element of a composite data type is again a composite one, the "CompositeTypeMapping" element will be used one more time (aggregation between the ArrayElementMapping and CompositeTypeMapping or aggregation between the RecordElementMapping and CompositeTypeMapping).

elements.name: argumentRef
elements.description:
Reference to an argument in the context of the mappedOperation. 
Only ClientServerCompositeTypeMapping elements that are directly aggregated by the ClientServerToSignalGroupMapping shall contain this reference.

ClientServerInterface.name: ClientServerInterface
ClientServerInterface.description: A client/server interface declares a number of operations that can be invoked on a server by a client.

elements.name: operations
elements.description:
ClientServerOperation(s) of this ClientServerInterface.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: possibleErrors
elements.description: Application errors that are defined as part of this interface.

ClientServerInterfaceMapping.name: ClientServerInterfaceMapping
ClientServerInterfaceMapping.description: Defines the mapping of ClientServerOperations in context of two different ClientServerInterfaces.

elements.name: errorMappings
elements.description: Map two different ApplicationErrors defined in the context of two different ClientServerInterfaces.

elements.name: operationMappings
elements.description: Mapping of two ClientServerOperations in two different ClientServerInterfaces

ClientServerOperation.name: ClientServerOperation
ClientServerOperation.description: An operation declared within the scope of a client/server interface.

elements.name: arguments
elements.description:
An argument of this ClientServerOperation
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: possibleErrorRefs
elements.description: Possible errors that may by raised by the referring operation.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

ClientServerOperationMapping.name: ClientServerOperationMapping
ClientServerOperationMapping.description: Defines the mapping of two particular ClientServerOperations in context of two different ClientServerInterfaces.

elements.name: argumentMappings
elements.description: Defines the mapping of two particular ArgumentDataPrototypes with unequal names or unequal semantic (resolution or range) in context of Operations.

elements.name: firstOperationRef
elements.description: First to-be-mapped ClientServerOperation of a ClientServerInterface.

elements.name: secondOperationRef
elements.description: Second to-be-mapped ClientServerOperation of a ClientServerInterface.

ClientServerPrimitiveTypeMapping.name: ClientServerPrimitiveTypeMapping
ClientServerPrimitiveTypeMapping.description: Mapping of an argument with a primitive datatype to a signal.

elements.name: argumentRef
elements.description: Reference to an argument in the context of the mappedOperation.

elements.name: systemSignalRef
elements.description: Reference to the system signal used to carry the argument

ClientServerRecordElementMapping.name: ClientServerRecordElementMapping
ClientServerRecordElementMapping.description:
Mapping of a primitive record element to a SystemSignal. If the ArgumentDataPrototype that is referenced by ClientServerCompositeTypeMapping is typed by an ApplicationDataType the reference to the ApplicationRecordElement shall be used. If the VariableDataPrototype is typed by the ImplementationDataType the reference to the ImplementationRecordElement shall be used. 

If the element is composite, there will be no mapping (multiplicity 0). In this case the "RecordElementMapping" Element will aggregate the "TypeMapping" Element. In that way also the composite datatypes can be mapped to SystemSignals. 

Regardless whether composite or primitive record element is mapped the record element always needs to be specified.

elements.name: applicationRecordElementRef
elements.description: Reference to a applicationRecordElement in the context of the mappedOperation or in the context of a composite element. This reference shall only be used if the ArgumentDataPrototype that is referenced by the ClientServerCompositeTypeMapping is typed by an ApplicationDataType.

elements.name: complexTypeMapping
elements.description: This aggregation will be used if the element is  composite.

elements.name: implementationRecordElementRef
elements.description: Reference to a ImplementationRecordElement in the context of the mappedOperation or in the context of a composite element. This reference shall only be used if the ArgumentDataPrototype that is referenced by the ClientServerCompositeTypeMapping is typed by an ImplementationDataType.

elements.name: systemSignalRef
elements.description: Reference to the system signal used to carry the primitive ApplicationRecordElement.

ClientServerRecordTypeMapping.name: ClientServerRecordTypeMapping
ClientServerRecordTypeMapping.description: If the ApplicationCompositeDataType is a Record, the "RecordTypeMapping" will be used.

elements.name: recordElementMappings
elements.description: Each ApplicationRecordElement must be mapped on a SystemSignal.

ClientServerToSignalGroupMapping.name: ClientServerToSignalGroupMapping
ClientServerToSignalGroupMapping.description:
This mapping is deprecated and will be removed in future. It is replaced by the ClientServerToSignalMapping.

Old description:
Mapping of client server operation arguments to signals of a signal group. Arguments with a primitive datatype will be mapped via the "ClientServerPrimitiveTypeMapping" element. 
Arguments with composite datatypes will be mapped via the "CompositeTypeMapping" element.

elements.name: applicationError
elements.description: In client server communication, the server may return any value within the application error range.

elements.name: clientId
elements.description: In case of a server on one ECU with multiple clients on other ECUs, the client server communication shall use different unique COM signals and signal groups for each client to allow the identification of the client associated with each system signal.

elements.name: compositeTypeMappings
elements.description: Mapping of arguments with composite datatypes.

elements.name: emptySignal
elements.description:
An emptySignal is created if no actual data is configured for a client-server communication, but if the RTE shall send a SignalGroup to initiate the communication.
An EmptySignalMapping shall only reference a SystemSignal that is referenced by an ISignal with length equal to zero.

elements.name: mappedOperationIref
elements.description: Reference to a Operation, which is mapped to a signal group.

elements.name: primitiveTypeMappings
elements.description: Mapping of an argument with a primitive datatype to a signal.

elements.name: requestGroupRef
elements.description: Reference to the signal group which contains the references to request signals used to transport the IN and INOUT arguments of the operation.

elements.name: responseGroupRef
elements.description: Reference to the signal group which contains the references to response signals used to transport the OUT and INOUT arguments of the operation.

elements.name: sequenceCounter
elements.description: The purpose of sequence counters is to map a response to the correct request of a known client.

ClientServerToSignalMapping.name: ClientServerToSignalMapping
ClientServerToSignalMapping.description: This element maps the ClientServerOperation to call- and return-SystemSignals. The serialization is defined by the referenced SerializationTechnology.

elements.name: callSignalRef
elements.description: Reference to the callSignal to which the IN and INOUT ArgumentDataPrototypes are mapped.

elements.name: clientServerOperationIref
elements.description: Reference to a ClientServerOperation, which is mapped to a call SystemSignal and a return SystemSignal.

elements.name: lengthClientId
elements.description:
This attribute defines the length of the used client identifier in bits.  If the attribute does not exist or its value is set to 0 this means that the client identifier is not used.

Please note that this attribute is deprecated and will be removed in future (Value is fixed to UInt16).

elements.name: lengthSequenceCounter
elements.description:
The purpose of a sequence counter is to map a response to the correct request of a known client. This attribute describes the length of the used sequence counter in bits. If the attribute does not exist or its value is set to 0 this means that the sequence counter is not used.

Please note that this attribute is deprecated and will be removed in future (Value is fixed to UInt16).

elements.name: returnSignalRef
elements.description: Reference to the returnSignal to which the OUT and INOUT ArgumentDataPrototypes are mapped.

elements.name: serializerRef
elements.description: The reference is set to obsolete. Use ISignal.dataTransformation instead.

Code.name: Code
Code.description: A generic code descriptor. The type of the code (source or object) is defined via the category attribute of the associated engineering object.

elements.name: artifactDescriptors
elements.description: Refers to the artifact belonging to this code descriptor.

elements.name: callbackHeaderRefs
elements.description:
The association callbackHeader describes in which header files the function declarations of callback functions are provided to a service module.
With this information the service module can include the appropriate header files in its configuration files.

CollectableElement.name: CollectableElement
CollectableElement.description:
This meta-class specifies the ability to be part of a specific  AUTOSAR collection of ARPackages or ARElements.

The scope of collection has been extended beyond CollectableElement with Revision 4.0.3. For compatibility reasons the name of this meta Class was not changed.

Collection.name: Collection
Collection.description:
This meta-class specifies a collection of elements. A collection can be utilized to express additional aspects for a set of elements. 

Note that Collection is an ARElement. Therefore it is applicable e.g. for EvaluatedVariant, even if this is not obvious.

Usually the category of a Collection is "SET". On the other hand, a Collection can also express an arbitrary relationship between elements. This is denoted by the category "RELATION" (see also [TPS_GST_00347]). 

In this case the collection represents an association from "sourceElement" to "targetElement" in the role "role".

elements.name: autoCollect
elements.description: This attribute reflects how far the referenced objects are part of the collection.

elements.name: elementRole
elements.description:
This attribute allows to denote a particular role of the collection. Note that the applicable semantics shall be mutually agreed between the two parties.

In particular it denotes the role of element in the context of sourceElement.

elements.name: elementRefs
elements.description:
This is an element in the collection. Note that Collection itself is collectable. Therefore collections can be nested.

In case of category="RELATION" this represents the target end of the relation.

elements.name: sourceElementRefs
elements.description: Only if Category = “RELATION”. This represents the source of a relation.

elements.name: collectedInstanceIrefs
elements.description: This instance ref supports the use case that a particular instance is part of the collection.

elements.name: sourceInstanceIrefs
elements.description: Only if Category = “RELATION”. This represents the source instance of a relation.

Colspec.name: Colspec
Colspec.description: This meta-class represents the ability to specify the properties of a column in a  table.

ComMgrUserNeeds.name: ComMgrUserNeeds
ComMgrUserNeeds.description: Specifies the abstract needs on the configuration of the Communication Manager for one "user".

elements.name: maxCommMode
elements.description: Maximum communication mode requested by this ComM user.

CommConnectorPort.name: CommConnectorPort
CommConnectorPort.description:
The Ecu communication relationship defines which signals, Pdus and frames are actually received and transmitted by this ECU. 

For each signal, Pdu or Frame that is transmitted or received and used by the Ecu an association between an ISignalPort, IPduPort or FramePort with the corresponding Triggering shall be created. 
An ISignalPort shall be created only if the corresponding signal is handled by COM (RTE or Signal Gateway). If a Pdu Gateway ECU only routes the Pdu without being interested in the content only a FramePort and an IPduPort needs to be created.

elements.name: communicationDirection
elements.description: Communication Direction of the Connector Port (input or output Port).

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

CommonSignalPath.name: CommonSignalPath
CommonSignalPath.description: The CommonSignalPath describes that two or more SwcToSwcSignals and/or SwcToSwcOperationArguments must take the same way (Signal Path) in the topology.

elements.name: signals
elements.description: The SwcToSwcSignals that must take the same way (Signal Path) in the topology.

CommunicationCluster.name: CommunicationCluster
CommunicationCluster.description:
The CommunicationCluster is the main element to describe the topological connection of communicating ECUs.

A cluster describes the ensemble of ECUs, which are linked by a communication medium of arbitrary topology (bus, star, ring, ...). The nodes within the cluster share the same communication protocol, which may be event-triggered, time-triggered or a combination of both.

A CommunicationCluster aggregates one or more physical channels.

CommunicationClusterContent.name: CommunicationClusterContent
CommunicationClusterContent.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

elements.name: baudrate
elements.description: Channels speed in bits/s.

elements.name: physicalChannels
elements.description:
This relationship defines which channel element belongs to which cluster. A channel must be assigned to exactly one cluster, whereas a cluster may have one or more channels.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: protocolName
elements.description: The name of the protocol used.

elements.name: protocolVersion
elements.description: The version of the protocol used.

elements.name: speed
elements.description:
This attribute is deprecated and is replaced by the attribute "baudrate". 

Old description: Channels speed in kbps.

CommunicationConnector.name: CommunicationConnector
CommunicationConnector.description:
The connection between the referencing ECU and the referenced channel via the referenced controller.

Connectors are used to describe the bus interfaces of the ECUs and to specify the sending/receiving behavior. 
Each CommunicationConnector has a reference to exactly one communicationController. 

Note: Several CommunicationConnectors can be assigned to one PhysicalChannel in the scope of one ECU Instance.

elements.name: commControllerRef
elements.description:
Reference to the communication controller.
The CommunicationConnector and referenced CommunicationController must be aggregated by the same ECUInstance. 

The communicationController can be referenced by several CommunicationConnector elements. This is important for the FlexRay Bus. FlexRay communicates via two physical channels. But only one controller in an ECU is responsible for both channels. Thus, two connectors (for channel A and for channel B) must reference to the same controller.

elements.name: ecuCommPortInstances
elements.description: The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: pncGatewayType
elements.description: Defines if this EcuInstance shall implement the PncGateway functionality on this CommunicationConnector and its respective PhysicalChannel. Several EcuInstances on the same PhysicalChannel can have the PncGateway functionality enabled, but only one of them shall have the pncGatewayType "active".

CommunicationConnectorRefConditional.name: CommunicationConnectorRefConditional
CommunicationConnectorRefConditional.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

CommunicationController.name: CommunicationController
CommunicationController.description: The communication controller is a dedicated hardware device by means of which hosts are sending frames to and receiving frames from the communication medium.

CommunicationControllerContent.name: CommunicationControllerContent
CommunicationControllerContent.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

elements.name: wakeUpByControllerSupported
elements.description:
Defines whether the ECU shall be woken up by this CommunicationController.
TRUE: wake up is possible
FALSE: wake up is not supported
Note: If wakeUpByControllerSupported is set to TRUE the feature shall be supported by both hardware and basic software.

CommunicationControllerMapping.name: CommunicationControllerMapping
CommunicationControllerMapping.description:
CommunicationControllerMapping specifies the CommunicationPeripheral
hardware (defined in the ECU Resource Template) to realize the specified CommunicationController in a physical topology.

elements.name: communicationControllerRef
elements.description: Reference to the CommunicationController in the System Template

elements.name: hwCommunicationControllerRef
elements.description: Reference to the hwCommunicationController in the ECU Resource Template.

CommunicationCycle.name: CommunicationCycle
CommunicationCycle.description: The communication cycle where the frame is sent.

Compiler.name: Compiler
Compiler.description: Specifies the compiler attributes. In case of source code this specifies requirements how the compiler shall be invoked. In case of object code this documents the used compiler settings.

elements.name: name
elements.description: Compiler name (like gcc).

elements.name: options
elements.description: Specifies the compiler options.

elements.name: vendor
elements.description: Vendor of compiler.

elements.name: version
elements.description: Exact version of compiler executable.

ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType.name: ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType
ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType.description: The ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType is a special AtomicSwComponentType that has direct access to hardware on an ECU and which is therefore linked to a specific ECU or specific hardware. The ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType introduces the possibility to link from the software representation to its hardware description provided by the ECU Resource Template.

elements.name: hardwareElementRefs
elements.description: Reference from the ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType to the description of the used HwElements.

ComponentClustering.name: ComponentClustering
ComponentClustering.description: Constraint that forces the mapping of all referenced SW component instances  to the same ECU, Core, Partition depending on the defined mappingScope attribute.  If mappingScope is not specified then mappingScopeEcu shall be assumed.

elements.name: clusteredComponentIrefs
elements.description: Reference to the components that have to be mapped together.

elements.name: mappingScope
elements.description: This attribute indicates whether the ComponentClustering mapping constraint applies to different ECUs, partitions or cores. If this attribute is not specified then mappingScopeEcu shall be assumed.

ComponentInCompositionInstanceRef.name: ComponentInCompositionInstanceRef
ComponentInCompositionInstanceRef.description: The ComponentInCompositionInstanceRef points to a concrete SwComponentPrototype within a CompositionSwComponentType.

ComponentSeparation.name: ComponentSeparation
ComponentSeparation.description:
Constraint that forces the two referenced SW components (called A and B in the following) not to be mapped to the same ECU, Core, Partition depending on the defined mappingScope attribute. If mappingScope is not specified then mappingScopeEcu shall be assumed. 

If a SW component (e.g. A) is a composition, none of the atomic SW components making up the A composition must be mapped together with any of the atomic SW components making up the B composition. Furthermore, A and B must be disjoint.

elements.name: mappingScope
elements.description: This attribute indicates whether the ComponentSeparation mapping constraint applies to different ECUs, partitions or cores. If this attribute is not specified then mappingScopeEcu shall be assumed.

elements.name: separatedComponentIrefs
elements.description: The two components that have to be mapped to different ECUs

CompositeNetworkRepresentation.name: CompositeNetworkRepresentation
CompositeNetworkRepresentation.description: This meta-class is used to define the network representation of leaf elements of composite application data types.

elements.name: leafElementIref
elements.description: This represents that leaf element of an application composite data type.

elements.name: networkRepresentation
elements.description: The SwDataDefProps owned by the CompositeNetworkRepresentation are used to define the network representation of the leaf element of an ApplicationCompositeDataType.

CompositionSwComponentType.name: CompositionSwComponentType
CompositionSwComponentType.description: A CompositionSwComponentType aggregates SwComponentPrototypes (that in turn are typed by SwComponentTypes) as well as SwConnectors for primarily connecting SwComponentPrototypes among each others and towards the surface of the CompositionSwComponentType. By this means hierarchical structures of software-components can be created.

elements.name: components
elements.description:
The instantiated components that are part of this composition.
The aggregation of SwComponentPrototype is subject to variability with the purpose to support the conditional existence of a SwComponentPrototype. Please be aware: if the conditional existence of SwComponentPrototypes is resolved post-build the deselected SwComponentPrototypes are still contained in the ECUs build but the instances are inactive in in that they are not scheduled by the RTE.

The aggregation is marked as atpSplitable in order to allow the addition of service components to the ECU extract during the ECU integration.

The use case for having 0 components owned by the CompositionSwComponentType could be to deliver an empty CompositionSwComponentType to e.g. a supplier for filling the internal structure.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: connectors
elements.description:
SwConnectors have the principal ability to establish a connection among PortPrototypes. They can have many roles in the context of a CompositionSwComponentType. Details are refined by subclasses.

The aggregation of SwConnectors is subject to variability with the purpose to support variant data flow.

The aggregation is marked as atpSplitable in order to allow the extension of the ECU extract with AssemblySwConnectors between ApplicationSwComponentTypes and ServiceSwComponentTypes during the ECU integration.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

elements.name: constantValueMappingRefs
elements.description: Reference to the ConstantSpecificationMapping to be applied for initValues of  PPortComSpecs and RPortComSpec.

elements.name: dataTypeMappingRefs
elements.description:
Reference to the DataTypeMapping to be applied for the used  ApplicationDataTypes in PortInterfaces.

Background: when developing subsystems it may happen that ApplicationDataTypes are used on the surface of CompositionSwComponentTypes. In this case it would be reasonable to be able to also provide the intended mapping to the ImplementationDataTypes. However, this mapping shall be informal and not technically binding for the implementers mainly because the RTE generator is not concerned about the CompositionSwComponentTypes. 

Rationale: if the mapping of ApplicationDataTypes on the delegated and inner
PortPrototype matches then the mapping to ImplementationDataTypes is not impacting compatibility.

elements.name: instantiationRteEventPropss
elements.description:
This allows to define instantiation specific properties for RTE Events, in particular for instance specific scheduling.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

Compu.name: Compu
Compu.description: This meta-class represents the ability to express one particular computation.

elements.name: compuDefaultValue
elements.description: This property can be used to specify an output value for a conversion formula, if the value to be converted lies outside the plausibility limit. Although this is possible for all conversion formulae, it is especially valid for variables with tabular conversion formulae.

elements.name: compuScales
elements.description:
This represents one scale within the compu method. Note that it contains a Variationpoint in order to support blueprints of enumerations.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

CompuConst.name: CompuConst
CompuConst.description: This meta-class represents the fact that the value of a computation method scale is constant.

elements.name: vf
elements.description:
Value calculated via a system constant. This element is included in every case where parameters should be generated from numerical values during compile time (not runtime!). 

Thus for example, the influence of the cylinder number on conversion formulae can be introduced in a repeatable manner.

elements.name: v
elements.description: This represents the numerical value.

elements.name: vt
elements.description: This represents a textual constant in the computation method.

CompuConstContent.name: CompuConstContent
CompuConstContent.description: This meta-class represents the fact that the constant value of the computation method can be numerical or textual.

CompuConstFormulaContent.name: CompuConstFormulaContent
CompuConstFormulaContent.description: This meta-class represents the fact that the constant value of the computation method is represented by a variation point. This difference is due to compatibility with ASAM HDO.

elements.name: vf
elements.description:
Value calculated via a system constant. This element is included in every case where parameters should be generated from numerical values during compile time (not runtime!). 

Thus for example, the influence of the cylinder number on conversion formulae can be introduced in a repeatable manner.

CompuConstNumericContent.name: CompuConstNumericContent
CompuConstNumericContent.description: This meta-class represents the fact that the constant value of the computation method is a numerical value. It is separated from CompuConstFormulaContent to support compatibility with ASAM HDO.

elements.name: v
elements.description: This represents the numerical value.

CompuConstTextContent.name: CompuConstTextContent
CompuConstTextContent.description: This meta-class represents the textual content of a scale.

elements.name: vt
elements.description: This represents a textual constant in the computation method.

CompuContent.name: CompuContent
CompuContent.description: This abstract meta-class represents the various definition means of a computation method.

CompuGenericMath.name: CompuGenericMath
CompuGenericMath.description: This meta-class represents the ability to specify a generic formula expression.

CompuMethod.name: CompuMethod
CompuMethod.description:
This meta-class represents the ability to express the relationship between a physical value and the mathematical representation. 

Note that this is still independent of the technical implementation in data types. It only specifies the formula how the internal value corresponds to its physical pendant.

elements.name: displayFormat
elements.description: This property specifies, how the physical value shall be displayed e.g. in documents or measurement and calibration tools.

elements.name: unitRef
elements.description: This is the physical unit of the Physical values for which the CompuMethod applies.

elements.name: compuInternalToPhys
elements.description: This specifies the computation from internal values to physical values.

elements.name: compuPhysToInternal
elements.description: This represents the computation from physical values to the internal values.

CompuNominatorDenominator.name: CompuNominatorDenominator
CompuNominatorDenominator.description: This class represents the ability to express a polynomial either as Nominator or as Denominator.

elements.name: v
elements.description: this is the list of polynomial factors. Note that the first vf represents the power=0.  The polynomial is v[0] * x^0 + v[1] * x^1 ...

CompuRationalCoeffs.name: CompuRationalCoeffs
CompuRationalCoeffs.description: This meta-class represents the ability to express a rational function by specifying the coefficients of nominator and denominator.

elements.name: compuNumerator
elements.description: This is the numerator of the rational expression.

elements.name: compuDenominator
elements.description: This is the denominator of the expression.

CompuScale.name: CompuScale
CompuScale.description: This meta-class represents the ability to specify one segment of a segmented computation method.

elements.name: shortLabel
elements.description: This element specifies a short name for the particular scale. The name can for example be used to derive a programming language identifier.

elements.name: symbol
elements.description: The symbol, if provided, is used by code generators to get a C identifier for the CompuScale. The name will be used as is for the code generation, therefore it needs to be unique within the generation context.

elements.name: desc
elements.description: <desc> represents a general but brief description of the object in question.

elements.name: mask
elements.description:
In difference to all the other computational methods every COMPU-SCALE will be applied including the bit MASK. Therefore it is allowed for this type of COMPU-METHOD, that COMPU-SCALES overlap. 

To calculate the string reverse to a value, the string has to be split and the according value for each substring has to be summed up. The sum is finally transmitted.

The processing has to be done in order of the COMPU-SCALE elements.

elements.name: lowerLimit
elements.description: This specifies the lower limit of the scale.

elements.name: upperLimit
elements.description: This specifies the upper limit of a of the scale.

elements.name: compuInverseValue
elements.description: This is the inverse value of the constraint. This supports the case that the scale is not reversible per se.

elements.name: variationPoint
elements.description: This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype.

elements.name: compuConst
elements.description: This represents the fact that the scale is a constant. The use case is mainly a non interplolated scale. It is a simplification of the fact that a constant scale can also be expressed as Rational Function of oder 0.

elements.name: compuRationalCoeffs
elements.description: This specifies the coefficients of the rational formula.

CompuScaleConstantContents.name: CompuScaleConstantContents
CompuScaleConstantContents.description: This meta-class represents the fact that a particular scale of the computation method is constant.

elements.name: compuConst
elements.description: This represents the fact that the scale is a constant. The use case is mainly a non interplolated scale. It is a simplification of the fact that a constant scale can also be expressed as Rational Function of oder 0.

CompuScaleContents.name: CompuScaleContents
CompuScaleContents.description: This abstract meta-class represents the content of one particular scale.

CompuScaleRationalFormula.name: CompuScaleRationalFormula
CompuScaleRationalFormula.description: This meta-class represents the fact that the computation in this scale is represented as rational term.

elements.name: compuRationalCoeffs
elements.description: This specifies the coefficients of the rational formula.

CompuScales.name: CompuScales
CompuScales.description: This meta-class represents the ability to stepwise express a computation method.

elements.name: compuScales

This represents one scale within the compu method. Note that it contains a Variationpoint in order to support blueprints of enumerations.
The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

ConcretePatternEventTriggering.name: ConcretePatternEventTriggering
ConcretePatternEventTriggering.description: The ConcretePatternEventTriggering describes the behavior of an event, which occurs following a precisely known pattern.

elements.name: patternJitter
elements.description: The optional parameter “Pattern Jitter” specifies the deviation of the time interval’s starting point from the beginning of the given period. This parameter is only applicable in conjunction with the parameter “Pattern Period”.

elements.name: patternPeriod
elements.description: The optional parameter “Pattern Period” specifies the time distance between the beginnings of subsequent repetitions of the given concrete pattern.

elements.name: offsets
elements.description: The offset for each occurrence of the event in the specified time interval.

elements.name: patternLength
elements.description: The length of the observed time interval.

ConditionByFormula.name: ConditionByFormula
ConditionByFormula.description:
This class represents a condition which is computed based on system constants according to the specified expression. The expected result is considered as boolean value.

The result of the expression is interpreted as a condition. 

* "0" represents "false";  

* a value other than zero is considered "true"

ConditionalChangeNad.name: ConditionalChangeNad
ConditionalChangeNad.description: Generates an conditional change NAD request. See LIN 2.1 protocol specification for more information.

elements.name: byte
elements.description: Byte Position of Data Byte that should be used for the bitwise XOR with Invert and the bitwise AND with Mask.

elements.name: id
elements.description: Byte Position of Id.

elements.name: invert
elements.description: Byte Position of Invert.

elements.name: mask
elements.description: Byte Position of Mask.

elements.name: newNad
elements.description: The newly assigned NAD value (Byte Position).

ConfidenceInterval.name: ConfidenceInterval
ConfidenceInterval.description: Additionally to the list of measured distances of event occurrences, a confidence interval can be specified for the expected distance of two consecutive event occurrences with a given probability.

elements.name: lowerBound
elements.description: The lower bound of the expected distance of two consecutive event occurrences.

elements.name: propability
elements.description: The probability for the measured lower and upper bound of the confidence interval.

elements.name: upperBound
elements.description: The upper bound of the expected distance of two consecutive event occurrences.

ConsistencyNeeds.name: ConsistencyNeeds
ConsistencyNeeds.description: This meta-class represents the ability to define requirements on the implicit communication behavior.

The upper multiplicity of this role has been increased to * due to resolving an atpVariation stereotype. The previous value was -1.

ConstantReference.description: Instead of defining this value inline, a constant is referenced.

ConstantSpecification.description: Specification of a constant that can be part of a package, i.e. it can be defined stand-alone.

ConstantSpecificationMapping.name: ConstantSpecificationMapping
ConstantSpecificationMapping.description:
This meta-class is used to create an association of two ConstantSpecifications. One ConstantSpecification is supposed to be defined in the application domain while the other should be defined in the implementation domain.

Hence the ConstantSpecificationMapping needs to be used where a ConstantSpecification defined in one domain needs to be associated to a ConstantSpecification in the other domain.

This information is crucial for the RTE generator.

elements.name: applConstantRef
elements.description: A ConstantSpecification defined in the application domain.

elements.name: implConstantRef
elements.description: A ConstantSpecification defined in the implementation domain.

ConstantSpecificationMappingSet.name: ConstantSpecificationMappingSet
ConstantSpecificationMappingSet.description: This meta-class represents the ability to map two ConstantSpecifications to each others. One ConstantSpecification is supposed to be described in the application domain and the other should be described in the implementation domain.

elements.name: mappings
elements.description: ConstantSpecificationMappings owned by the ConstantSpecificationMappingSet.

ConsumedEventGroup.name: ConsumedEventGroup
ConsumedEventGroup.description: A Service may have event groups which can be consumed. A service consumer has to subscribe to the corresponding event-group. After the subscription the event consumer takes the role of a server and the event provider that of a client.

elements.name: applicationEndpointRef
elements.description: Defines the application endpoint where the events of the event group are received. This may be a different TpPort address (ApplicationEndpoint) then that which is used for the sending of requests.

elements.name: eventGroupIdentifier
elements.description: EventGroup ID. Shall be unique within one system to allow service discovery.

elements.name: instanceIdentifier
elements.description: Instance identifier. Can be used for e.g. service discovery to identify the instance of the event group.

elements.name: priority
elements.description: Priority defined per consumed Event-Group

elements.name: routingGroupRefs
elements.description: The ServiceDiscovery module is able to activate and deactivate the PDU routing for receiving events.

elements.name: sdClientConfig
elements.description: The readiness to receive events is defined by the ServiceDiscovery of the ConsumedEventGroup. The EventHandler shall know about this announcement to decide about the submission of events. Therefore the EventHandler may be configured with Service-Discovery Client attributes.

ConsumedServiceInstance.name: ConsumedServiceInstance
ConsumedServiceInstance.description: Service instances that are consumed by the ECU that is connected via the ApplicationEndpoint to a CommunicationConnector.

elements.name: consumedEventGroups
elements.description: Selection of event-groups the consumer wants to subscribe for.

elements.name: providedServiceInstanceRef
elements.description: Reference to a providedServiceInstance to get the instanceIdentifier information from the ProvidedServiceInstance.

elements.name: sdClientConfig
elements.description: Service Discovery Client configuration.

ContainedIPduProps.name: ContainedIPduProps
ContainedIPduProps.description: Defines the aspects of an IPdu which can be collected inside a ContainerIPdu.

elements.name: collectionSemantics
elements.description: Defines whether this ContainedIPdu shall be collected using a last-is-best or queued semantics.

elements.name: headerIdLongHeader
elements.description: Defines the header id this IPdu shall have in case this IPdu is put inside a ContainerIPdu with headerType = longHeader.

elements.name: headerIdShortHeader
elements.description: Defines the header id this IPdu shall have in case this IPdu is put inside a ContainerIPdu with headerType = shortHeader.

elements.name: timeout
elements.description: Defines a IPdu specific sender timeout which can reduce the ContainerIPdu timer when this containedIPdu is put inside the ContainerIPdu. This attribute is ignored on receiver side.

elements.name: trigger
elements.description:
Defines whether this IPdu does trigger the sending of the ContainerIPdu.
This attribute is ignored on receiver side.

ContainerIPdu.name: ContainerIPdu
ContainerIPdu.description: Allows to collect several IPdus in one ContainerIPdu based on the IPdu.headerId.

elements.name: containedPduTriggeringRefs
elements.description: This PduTriggering shall be collected inside the ContainerIPdu.

elements.name: containerTimeout
elements.description:
When this timeout expires the ContainerIPdu is sent out. The respective timer is started when the first Ipdu is put into the ContainerIPdu.
This attribute is ignored on receiver side.

elements.name: containerTrigger
elements.description: Defines if the transmission of the ContainerIPdu shall be requested right after the first ContainedIPdu was put into it. This attribute shall be ignored on receiver side.

elements.name: headerType
elements.description: Defines the type and size of the header information (header id and length).

elements.name: rxAcceptContainedIPdu
elements.description: Defines whether this ContainerIPdu has a fixed set of containedIPdus assigned for reception.

elements.name: thresholdSize
elements.description: Defines the size threshold which, when exceeded, triggers the sending of the ContainerIPdu although the maxium Pdu size has not been reached yet. Unit: byte.

CouplingElement.name: CouplingElement
CouplingElement.description: A CouplingElement is used to connect EcuInstances to the VLAN of an EthernetCluster. CouplingElements can reach from a simple hub to a complex managed switch or even devices with functionalities in higher layers. A CouplingElement that is not related to an EcuInstance occurs as a dedicated single device.

elements.name: communicationClusterRef
elements.description: This relationship defines to which cluster the CouplingElement belongs.

elements.name: couplingPorts
elements.description: Hardware Port of the CouplingElement that is used to connect this CouplingPort to EcuInstances or other CouplingElements.

elements.name: couplingType
elements.description: Describes the coupling type of this CouplingElement.

elements.name: ecuInstanceRef
elements.description: Optional reference to the ECU where the CouplingElement is located.

CouplingPort.name: CouplingPort
CouplingPort.description: A CouplingPort is used to connect a CouplingElement with an EcuInstance or two CouplingElements with each other via a CouplingPortConnection. Optionally, the CouplingPort may also have a reference to a macMulticastGroup and a defaultVLAN.

elements.name: connectionNegotiationBehavior
elements.description: Specifies the connection negotiation of the CouplingPort.

elements.name: couplingPortDetails
elements.description: Defines more details of a CouplingPort in case a more specific configuration is required.

elements.name: couplingPortSpeed
elements.description: CouplingPort speed in bits/s.

elements.name: defaultVlanRef
elements.description:
The vLanIdentifier of the referenced VLAN is the Default-PVID (port VLAN ID). A Port VLAN ID is a default VLAN ID that is assigned to an access CouplingPort to designate the VLAN segment to which this port is connected. Also, if a CouplingPort has not been configured with any VLAN memberships, the virtual switch's Port VLAN ID (pvid) becomes the default VLAN ID for the ports connection.

This identifier/tag is added for incoming untagged messages at the port (ingress tagging). For outgoing messages with this identifier, the tag is removed at the port (egress untagging, depending on the VlanMembership.sendActivity).

elements.name: macMulticastAddressRefs
elements.description: Static MAC-Multicast-Address binding to a CouplingPort. This supports the sending of MAC-Multicast-Messages via the CouplingPort.

elements.name: physicalLayerType
elements.description: Specifies the physical layer type of the CouplingPort.

elements.name: vlanMemberships
elements.description: Messages of VLANs that are defined here can be communicated via the CouplingPort.

elements.name: vlanModifierRef
elements.description:
All incoming messages at this CouplingPort shall be tagged with this VLAN Id. This tagging is performed regardless whether the message already has a VLAN tag or is untagged, an existing VLAN tag will be overwritten.

This feature is XOR with CoupligPort.defaultVlan.

CouplingPortConnection.name: CouplingPortConnection
CouplingPortConnection.description: Connection between two CouplingPorts (firstPort and secondPort).

elements.name: firstPortRef
elements.description: Reference to the first CouplingPort that is connected via the CouplingPortConnection.

elements.name: secondPortRef
elements.description: Reference to the second CouplingPort that is connected via the CouplingPortConnection.

CouplingPortDetails.name: CouplingPortDetails
CouplingPortDetails.description:
Defines details of a CouplingPort.

May be used to configure the structures of a switch.

elements.name: couplingPortStructuralElements
elements.description: Collects all the structural parts at which a CouplingPort may be configurable.

elements.name: ethernetPriorityRegenerations
elements.description: Defines a priority regeneration where the ingress priority is replaced by regenerated priority.

elements.name: ethernetTrafficClassAssignments
elements.description: Defines the ingress port to EthernetTrafficClass assignment.

elements.name: lastEgressSchedulerRef
elements.description: Defines which CouplingPortScheduler is the last in the egress port structure.

CouplingPortFifo.name: CouplingPortFifo
CouplingPortFifo.description: Defines a Fifo for the CouplingPort egress structure.

elements.name: assignedTrafficClasss
elements.description:
Defines a set of Traffic Classes which shall be handled by this Fifo.

range: 0-7

CouplingPortScheduler.name: CouplingPortScheduler
CouplingPortScheduler.description: Defines a scheduler for the CouplingPort egress structure.

elements.name: portScheduler
elements.description: Defines the schedule algorithm to be used.

elements.name: predecessorRefs
elements.description: Ordered List of predecessor inputs. The first element has the highest priority. The following elements have decreasing priorities.

CouplingPortShaper.name: CouplingPortShaper
CouplingPortShaper.description: Defines a shaper for the CouplingPort egress structure.

elements.name: idleSlope
elements.description: Defines the increase of credit in bits per second for the AVB shaper.

elements.name: predecessorFifoRef
elements.description: Defines the CouplingPortFifo which provides the input to this shaper.

CouplingPortStructuralElement.name: CouplingPortStructuralElement
CouplingPortStructuralElement.description: General class to define structural elements a CouplingPort may consist of.

CouplingPortTrafficClassAssignment.name: CouplingPortTrafficClassAssignment
CouplingPortTrafficClassAssignment.description:
Defines the assignment of Traffic Class to a frame.

Two use-cases are supported:
1. Only one ethernetTrafficClassAssignment is defined and NO priority is given:
--> all frames on this ingress port get assigned the trafficClass.
2. for each ethernetTrafficClass WITH a priority the frames which are coming in with this priority get assigned the trafficClass.

Constraint: 1 and 2 can not be combined for one CouplingPortDetails.

elements.name: prioritys
elements.description: Defines a priority which is mapped onto a Traffic Class.

elements.name: trafficClass
elements.description:
Defines the Traffic Class which is assigned.

range: 0-7

CryptoServiceNeeds.name: CryptoServiceNeeds
CryptoServiceNeeds.description: Specifies the needs on the configuration of the CryptoServiceManager for one ConfigID (see Specification AUTOSAR_SWS_CSM.doc). An instance of this class is used to find out which ports of an SWC belong to this ConfigID.

elements.name: maximumKeyLength
elements.description: The maximum length of a cryptographic key, that is used by the SWC or module for this configuration.  Unit: bit.

CycleCounter.name: CycleCounter
CycleCounter.description: The communication cycle where the frame is send is described by the attribute "cycleCounter".

elements.name: cycleCounter
elements.description:
The communication cycle where the frame described by this timing is sent. If a timing is given in this way the referencing FlexrayCluster shall specify the cycleCountMax as upper bound and point of total repetition.
This value is incremented at the beginning of each new cycle, ranging from 0 to cycleCountMax, and is reset to 0 after a sequence of cycleCountMax+1 cycles.

CycleRepetition.name: CycleRepetition
CycleRepetition.description:
The communication cycle where the frame is send is described by the
attributes baseCycle and cycleRepetition.

elements.name: baseCycle
elements.description:
The first communication cycle where the frame is sent.

This value is incremented at the beginning of each new cycle, ranging from 0 to
63, and is reset to 0 after a sequence of 64 cycles.

elements.name: cycleRepetition
elements.description: The number of communication cycles (after the first cycle) whenever the frame described by this timing is sent again.

CyclicTiming.name: CyclicTiming
CyclicTiming.description: Specification of a cyclic sending behavior.

elements.name: timeOffset
elements.description: This attribute specifies the time until first transmission of this I-PDU. This attribute defines the time between Com_IpduGroupStart and the first transmission of the cyclic part of this transmission request for this I-PDU.

elements.name: timePeriod
elements.description: Period of the repetition of cyclic transmissions.

DataConstr.name: DataConstr

DataPrototypeMapping.name: DataPrototypeMapping
DataPrototypeMapping.description:
Defines the mapping of two particular VariableDataPrototypes, ParameterDataPrototypes or ArgumentDataPrototypes with unequal names and/or unequal semantic (resolution or range) in context of two different SenderReceiverInterface, NvDataInterface or ParameterInterface or Operations.

If the semantic is unequal following rules apply:
The textTableMapping is only applicable if the referred DataPrototypes are typed by AutosarDataType referring to CompuMethods of category TEXTTABLE, SCALE_LINEAR_AND_TEXTTABLE or BITFIELD_TEXTTABLE.

In the case that the  DataPrototypes are typed by AutosarDataType either referring to CompuMethods of category LINEAR, IDENTICAL or referring to no CompuMethod (which is similar as  IDENTICAL) the linear conversion factor is calculated out of the factorSiToUnit and offsetSiToUnit attributes of the referred Units and the CompuRationalCoeffs of a compuInternalToPhys of the referred CompuMethods.

elements.description: First to be mapped DataPrototype in context of a  SenderReceiverInterface, NvDataInterface, ParameterInterface or Operation.

And to execute the DataTransformation <Mip>_Inv_<transformerId> functions of the transformation chain when communicating from the DataPrototypeMapping.secondDataPrototype to the DataPrototypeMapping.firstDataPrototype.
